Checked on a Windows 11 x64 PC (2026-11-16) with a self-signed test certificate, removed afterwards: release-windows.ps1 -SignCommand … builds a signed setup and a signed MSIX (both binaries inside signed; MakeAppx accepts the manifest); install.ps1 with the local MSIX checks checksum and publisher and installs it; gitoodo --version runs through the alias; gitoodo service install from the packaged command puts the stable copy into the real %LOCALAPPDATA%\de.gitoodo.app\bin and starts Gitoodo\Daemon ; Credential Manager is read from the package ( token-access → readable ); the app runs with its package identity and writes only to the real data folders (nothing in the package's LocalCache ); the App Installer file registers its update settings; switching MSIX → setup → MSIX keeps services, settings and tokens; uninstall.ps1 removes all of it and -Check finds nothing. Not checked: the startup task and notifications in the UI, an update from a newer .appinstaller over HTTPS. Add-AppxPackage needs an interactive sign-in session (over SSH it fails with 0x80070005 ). Homebrew and winget (prepared, not published) Both are written from the release's releases.json , so they always name the files and checksums that were really published: python3 scripts/package-managers.py target/release/dist/releases.json # -> target/release/packages Homebrew: packaging/homebrew/gitoodo.rb is the cask template in the usual style of a project's own tap: the versioned DMG URL, livecheck on the latest GitHub release, Apple silicon only, the gitoodo command as binary , uninstall launchctl: for the LaunchAgents and a zap list. The script writes packages/homebrew/Casks/gitoodo.rb with version and sha256 of downloads.mac (and refuses a DMG that is not notarized or whose URL differs from the template). The tap is the repository silvio-l/homebrew-gitoodo ( brew install --cask silvio-l/gitoodo/gitoodo ); its README is packaging/homebrew/README.md . Once: create the repository with that README. Per release: commit the new Casks/gitoodo.rb , then on a clean Mac brew audit --cask --online silvio-l/gitoodo/gitoodo , brew install --cask silvio-l/gitoodo/gitoodo , start the app, brew uninstall --cask gitoodo (stops the LaunchAgents). The official homebrew/cask comes later (notability rules). winget: the script writes the three manifests (schema 1.9.0) of Gitoodo.Gitoodo for the per-user NSIS setup ( downloads.windowsSetup , InstallerType: nullsoft , Scope: user , silent /S is the NSIS default) to packages/winget/manifests/g/Gitoodo/Gitoodo/<version>/ . The identifier is the product's, never a person's name ( scripts/check-identifier.py ). Per release: winget validate --manifest <dir> and winget install --manifest <dir> in Windows Sandbox ( winget settings --enable LocalManifestFiles once), then one pull request with that folder to microsoft/winget-pkgs . The setup is unsigned for now; winget checks the checksum and the scanners of the winget pipeline decide, Microsoft may refuse it. When the MSIX is signed, a second installer entry ( InstallerType: msix ) can follow. bash scripts/package-managers.test.sh (part of ci-gates.sh ) checks the script and, with brew installed, runs brew style on the written cask. App identifier (decision 2026-11-16, #595) Gitoodo is de.gitoodo.app on every system: bundle ID, keychain group Q7V3X27S2U.de.gitoodo.app , service helper de.gitoodo.app.service , launchd labels de.gitoodo.app.{daemon,dispatcher} , folders, MSIX identity and AUMID, test build de.gitoodo.app.testaccess . It is written once per language: app_identifier! in crates/core/src/paths.rs (Rust derives labels, groups and paths from it), identifier in src-tauri/tauri.conf.json (Tauri, package.ps1 , release-windows.ps1 , build-local-mac.sh ), and the identifier variables of the install and uninstall scripts. Files that cannot derive it (Info.plists, entitlements, LaunchAgents, cask) are held equal by scripts/check-identifier.py in the gates and src-tauri/src/identity_files.rs ; the gate also fails on any identifier built from a person's name. Gitoodo 0.1.x used online.lindstedt.gitoodo . The first start of a newer direct build moves everything once ( crates/core/src/identity_migration.rs ): it stops and removes the old login items/LaunchAgents (Windows: scheduled tasks, Linux: user units), moves settings, state, logs, web data and the stable CLI copy (a rename; when the new folder already exists, entry by entry, never overwriting), copies the keychain tokens from the old access group into the new one, reads them back and only then deletes the old items, and registers the services again under the new labels with their previous on/off state. It is idempotent and safe to interrupt; it logs what it moved, never a value. The CLI moves the folders on service , status , doctor and diagnose for headless installs. Not moved: preferences and caches (rebuilt), the store and test builds. uninstall.sh , uninstall.ps1 and the cask remove both identifiers' leftovers. The App Installer of a 0.1.x MSIX cannot update across identities: such installs update by running install.ps1 again, which installs the new package and removes the old one (write virtualization is off, so no data goes with it). Checked on macOS on 2026-11-19 (#837) with Developer-ID-signed dev builds over a configured 0.1.x install, the first start killed after 0.3 s: the next start finished the move without re-setup or data loss, the running classifier came back under de.gitoodo.app.daemon , both keychain items moved and the services read them without a dialog. Known gaps: an installed but stopped service is not carried over and the old login items stay listed until the old bundle is gone (both by design and named in the move's log notes, #1248, see permissions ), the kept-entries note can be lost when the first start is interrupted, and macOS asks again for folder access

h: A block the human can decide from alone
b: This document is the single source of truth for the format that agents use to ask a human a question in a forge issue or comment, and for the answer comment that Gitoodo posts back. The parsers ( src/question/ and crates/core/src/question.rs ), the agent skill ( skill/gitoodo-questions/SKILL.md ) and the tests follow it. The examples below are extracted and parsed by a test, so they cannot drift from the parsers. Both question parsers read the examples directly from this document and compare their complete results against tests/question-examples.expected.json . When changing the format, update the examples and their shared expected results together; do not copy example inputs into another fixture. Version 2 replaces version 1; v1 blocks and answers are no longer read. The machine-read parts are fixed and English (markers, kind , Deadline: , Recommendation: , (yes/no) , (multiple) , (text) , the answer tokens yes , no , explain , other ). The human-read parts (the header line, context, questions, option labels, consequences, reasons) are written in the language Gitoodo writes in on the forge (en, de, es, ar, hi, zh-Hans): the setting "Language on the forge" (the app language, English, the issue's language or a fixed language), which a repository can override. "The issue's language" is read from the issue's title and body without code, links and mentions; when the text is short, mixed or in another language, the app language is used. Readers never depend on that language: answers are understood in every supported language ( yes , ja , sí , نعم , हाँ , 是 , …; see "Answer comment"). The format is an open standard: any agent, tool or forge integration may write and read it without Gitoodo. Its public, versioned home is https://gitoodo.com/spec/questions/v2/ , generated from this document when the site is built. Section anchors are the GitHub-style slugs of the headings ( #answer-comment , #tolerant-reading , #plain-answers ), so links into this document work the same in the repository and on the site. Compatibility promise Version 2 is stable. Within version 2 these never break: A block or answer comment that follows the exact grammar of this document stays valid and keeps its meaning: the markers, v2 , the id and kind attributes, the header, context, Deadline: , question, option and Recommendation: lines, the kind suffixes and the answer tokens ( 1b , 2 yes , 3 "text" , explain , 1 other "text" ). The machine-read parts stay English and keep their spelling; the block kinds worker , approval and clarification keep their meaning. A reader never demands more than this document demands today, so a writer that follows it is understood by every version 2 reader. The rule for detecting an answered question stays the same, and the forge remains the only source of truth. The one clarification (#764): a comment carrying a Gitoodo machine marker is never the human's reply, even under the human's login (see "Gitoodo comments"). The URL above and its section anchors stay valid for as long as version 2 exists. What may change within version 2: Tolerant reading may accept more slips, words and languages. It never changes how an exact block is read. Explanations, examples and the wording of this document may be clarified without changing a rule. How an app presents a card (layout, hints, controls) is not part of the format. Anything that would break a valid version 2 block or answer gets a new version with its own marker ( v3 ) and its own URL ( /spec/questions/v3/ ). The version 2 page stays published with its rules unchanged. Design goals Works on Forgejo, Gitea, GitHub and GitLab without any server-side support. Reads well as plain Markdown when the app is not used (a human can answer with a normal comment). Machine-readable: the app renders an answer card, the agent parses the answer. Agents write the exact format below; the app reads leniently (see "Tolerant reading") so that slips, hand-written questions and plain human answers still work. Anything that is not clearly a question stays plain text. Nothing ever crashes or half-renders. Question block A block is delimited by two HTML comments. HTML comments are invisible in the rendered Markdown of all four forges, and the text between them renders as normal Markdown (a numbered list with the options as lines below each item). <!-- gitoodo:questions v2 id="<id>" kind="<kind>" --> @<login> **<Name>** (<hint how to answer, e.g. `1b` or `2 yes`>) <up to 3 context lines> Deadline: <YYYY-MM-DD> 1. <Question>? a) <Option> – <consequence> b) <Option> – <consequence> Recommendation: a 2. <Question>? (yes/no) Recommendation: yes <!-- /gitoodo:questions --> Delimiters Opening: <!-- gitoodo:questions v2 id="<id>" kind="<kind>" --> . v2 is the format version; <id> matches [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64} and identifies the block inside its issue. The answer repeats it. <kind> is worker , approval or clarification (see "Block kinds"); both attributes are required, in this order. Closing: <!-- /gitoodo:questions --> . A body may contain several blocks. Ids must be unique per issue; for a repeated id the first block wins. Blocks inside fenced code blocks (``` or ~~~) are ignored, so documentation can quote the format. Block kinds The kind tells the orchestrator (and the app) why the question is asked. It never changes how the block is parsed or answered; the parsed block carries it as kind next to id . Kind Asked by Meaning worker an agent working on the issue The worker is blocked on a human decision and continues after it. approval the classifier A yes/no gate, e.g. for an issue or PR of an untrusted author. clarification the classifier The issue is contradictory or unclear ( needs-clarification ). Unmarked questions (found in running text) have the kind worker . Who is asked A worker never picks the addressee. Each account has one setting, "Agents' questions go to" (Settings → Accounts and the account step of the onboarding; by default the account's own login, the user the token belongs to; for a bot or worker account the app asks instead of assuming). A repository's human and its routing rules override it there. gitoodo ask writes that person into the header; a to that is none of these people (a placeholder such as human , a guess such as x , the agent account that opened the issue) is replaced. "Questions for me", the notifications and the answer detection use the same setting: a worker card in a repository with Autopilot rules that names nobody of these people, and any card that names a placeholder, is read as addressed to the person who decides, so it shows and that person's reply answers it. A card someone forwarded on purpose keeps its addressee. The issue's assignees and its author never decide who is asked: they are often the worker or an agent account. The hint how to answer ( answer like … ) is written in the language Gitoodo writes in on that issue (the repository's forge language, else the app setting), whatever language the worker started its spec in. An issue with an open question is never shown as stuck: it waits in "Questions for me" with its question, also while its labels still say stalled . "Stuck" is only for an issue whose runs and resolver neither solved it nor asked. gitoodo ask --check tests a spec and prints the block without posting it. A block whose id is already on the issue is refused, so a retry or a probe never posts the same question twice. Content All lines are optional, except at least one question. Part Syntax Notes Header @<login> **<Name>** (…) First line. Addresses the human; text after the bold part is free. A login that is no trusted person of the repo (unknown on the forge, no write access) counts as addressed to the user who reads the questions. Context up to 3 plain lines between header and first question More than 3 makes the block invalid. Deadline Deadline: YYYY-MM-DD Among the context lines; does not count as one. At most once. Question <n>. <text> with n = 1, 2, 3, 4 in order 1 to 4 questions per block. Option a) <label> or a) <label> – <consequence> Keys a to d in order. The dash is an en dash or - . Recommendation Recommendation: <value> below the question At most once. Agents should always give one (see the skill). Question kinds The kind is given by an optional suffix at the end of the question line. Kind Suffix Options Recommendation: value Answer token single choice none 2 to 4 ( a to d ) one key, e.g. a 1b or 1bc multiple choice (multiple) 2 to 4 ( a to d ) keys separated by commas: a, c 1ac yes/no (yes/no) none yes or no 2 yes free text (text) none not allowed 3 "any text" A recommendation may be followed by – <reason> ; the reason is ignored. A single choice asks for one option, but the human may combine several: a click in the app picks one option, and an option can be added on purpose (the card's "choose several" control or a Cmd/Ctrl-click). The answer then carries every chosen key like a multiple choice ( 1bc ). Agents read such an answer as "all of these options" (see the skill). The question block itself is unchanged: a single choice still has at most one recommended key. Answer comment The app posts one comment per answered block: <!-- gitoodo:answer v2 id="<id>" --> <answer line> <optional free text, Markdown> Line 1 is the marker with the same id as the block. Line 2 is the answer line: space-separated tokens, one per answered question, in question order: single or multiple choice: number plus the chosen keys in alphabetical order, no separator: 1b , 3ac ; yes/no: number, a space, yes or no : 2 yes ; free text: number, a space, then the text as a double-quoted JSON string ( \" and \n escapes): 4 "Berlin" ; "please explain better", for every kind: number, a space, explain , optionally a space and a note what is unclear as a double-quoted JSON string: 2 explain or 2 explain "What does staging mean here?" (see "Explanation requests"); "none of these fits", for single and multiple choice: number, a space, other , a space and the person's own answer as a non-empty double-quoted JSON string: 1 other "Only test it internally first" (see "Own answers"). Questions can be left out (partial answers are valid). Each number occurs at most once. After one blank line follows optional free text, the person's note ("Anmerkung"). It is plain Markdown and not interpreted (see "Notes"). An answer line that does not match this grammar makes the whole comment "not an answer" (it stays an ordinary comment). The tokens are case-insensitive when parsed; the app always writes the lowercase English tokens. Every supported language is understood when reading, in the answer comment and in plain answers: Meaning Words yes yes , ja , sí , si , نعم , हाँ , हां , 是 , 好 no no , nein , لا , नहीं , नही , 否 , 不 explain explain , erklären , explicar , اشرح , समझाएं , 解释 other other , anders , andere , otro , otra , أخرى , آخر , अन्य , 其他 A word ends at whitespace, , , ; , . or a quote; digits and keys ( 1ac ) stay as described above. Explanation requests Instead of choosing, the human can send a single question back with <n> explain when the question, the options or the decision criteria are not understood. It is allowed for every question kind and can be combined with answers to the other questions of the same block ( 1b 2 explain "What does b cost?" 3 yes ). The optional note is a JSON string like a free-text answer; an empty note is written as no note. The agent re-asks exactly the questions marked explain in a new block (new id ) with a fuller explanation of the question, the options and the decision criteria, and keeps the other questions as answered. For the app the block counts as answered like after any other partial answer, so the question is no longer open until the new block arrives, which then shows up as a new question. Own answers When none of the options of a single or multiple choice fits, the human answers that question with <n> other "…" and writes what they want instead (#1200). The text is required and replaces e

Every subcommand of the gitoodo command line, generated from the text gitoodo --help prints (the USAGE constant in crates/cli/src/main.rs ). The app installs the command with its background services; the daemon reference covers configuration and tokens. Synopsis usage: gitoodo <command> [options] (gitoodo <command> --help shows one command) docs: https://gitoodo.com/docs/dev/cli/ Everyday: gitoodo status [--changed] [--json] [--ack] queue picture of all configured accounts: what waits for you and what the workers do --changed exit 0 when the lines that wait for a person changed since the last --ack, 1 otherwise exit 3 when the last poll could not read an account (the summary counts it) or the config --json machine-readable output; --ack remembers the current lines as seen gitoodo stop-all emergency stop: no new work, running workers are stopped and released (worktrees kept), no merges and no classifier writes until `gitoodo resume`; survives restarts gitoodo resume lift the emergency stop; every repo continues in the state it had before gitoodo attach [--host <name>] <issue> terminal of a worker, raw mode, detach with Ctrl-]; the worker keeps running gitoodo usage [--refresh] [--json] usage limits of the coding agents (5-hour and weekly window, paused until); --refresh checks every agent on every machine now (at most every 30 s), a lifted limit starts workers at once gitoodo --version print the CLI version (the app compares it with its own) Diagnosis: gitoodo doctor diagnostics: where the daemon takes tokens from (systemd credentials, service environment, system keyring or memory only) and, per account, whether this terminal reads the token; when the keychain wants approval it names the ways on: the app's System check, token-access --grant, or GITOODO_TOKEN_<ID> gitoodo restore-config replace a broken orchestration.json with the last valid copy Gitoodo saved (orchestration.json.bak); the broken file is kept as orchestration.json.corrupt gitoodo trace <owner/repo#n | run-id> [--local] [--output] timeline of one issue or run from the logs: every step from the classifier's decision over host choice, worktree, worker, pull request and checks to merge and cleanup, with durations; also asks the worker machines for their lines (--local: this machine only); read-only, redacted; names the worker transcripts kept on this machine (--output: prints them) gitoodo diagnose [--hours <n>] summary of the last 24 hours (or n): runs, count and p50/p95 per step, top wait reasons, errors by kind, the log folder against its budget and the cleanup state (leftover worktrees and branches, disk, errors); read-only, redacted gitoodo token-access --account <id> [--grant] whether the background services read the account's token without a keychain prompt; prints readable, needsPrompt, missing or failed; --grant asks once so "Always Allow" can be chosen gitoodo clean [--dry-run] remove what coding agents keep of Gitoodo's runs whose worktree is gone (session transcripts, project and state folders), as the dispatcher does every round; --dry-run only lists it. The user's own sessions and the data of runs that may resume stay gitoodo autoclean [--plan] [--disk-low] one pass of the automatic disk cleanup the dispatcher runs on its schedule (caches of installed tools, build output of managed repositories, old temp files); --plan checks everything and removes nothing, --disk-low applies the rules for a full disk Releases and setup: gitoodo release [--repo <owner/name>] [--json] release planning: open, in-progress and merged items of the next release (https://gitoodo.com/docs/dev/release-planning/) gitoodo release-version --repo <owner/name> [--account <id>] [--json] [--check] suggested next version from the next release's issues and the last released version, with its reason; a script scheme runs the repo's script in the local checkout without a token; --check only checks the stored version config gitoodo release-rules --repo <owner/name> [--account <id>] [--json] release assignment rules in effect, their problems and the suggestions waiting for approval; read only, the rules are edited in the app gitoodo release-runs [--repo <owner/name>] [--account <id>] [--json] completed releases and the state of their automation steps; read only, releases are completed and steps retried or skipped in the app gitoodo labels migrate <account> <owner/repo> [--yes] switch an active repo from legacy label names to the catalog by renaming (issues keep their labels); prints the preview and changes nothing without --yes; same in the app: Settings › Repos › <repo> › Migrate old labels… (when this terminal may not read the token: token-access --grant, or GITOODO_TOKEN_<ID> in the command's environment) gitoodo account add --forge forgejo|gitea|github|gitlab --url <url> --token-stdin [--label <name>] [--id <id>] [--store keyring|credential] gitoodo account token <account> --token-stdin [--store keyring|credential] | list | remove <account> forge accounts without the app (a server without a desktop): the token comes on stdin only (typed hidden on a terminal), is checked with the forge and kept in the system keyring or, where none answers (headless Linux), as a systemd credential both services load (a file only you can read in the state folder plus a drop-in per service, which this writes) gitoodo repo list <account> | activate <account> <owner/repo> [--backlog ask|ready|new] [--paused] gitoodo repo pause|observe <account> <owner/repo> the repository switch without the app: list shows each repository's state; activate shows the label changes and what happens to open issues per backlog choice and writes nothing until --backlog is given, then creates the labels and switches the repo on (--paused: labels and comments, no workers); an account is named by id, label or login gitoodo host add <name> <ssh-target> | list | remove <name> configure worker machines (satellites: other computers that run workers for this one over SSH); ssh target only, no secrets gitoodo memory list [--repo <owner/name> [--account <id>] | --global] [--kind <kind>] [--status active|proposed|disputed|archived|all] [--json] gitoodo memory show|archive|remove <id> [--json] gitoodo memory add --kind fact|procedure|preference|location [--repo <owner/name> [--account <id>]] [--origin human|worker|optimization] [--status active|proposed] [--pin] (<text> | --text-stdin) [--json] gitoodo memory edit <id> [--text <text> | --text-stdin] [--kind <kind>] [--repo <owner/name> [--account <id>] | --global] [--status <status>] [--pin|--unpin] [--json] knowledge Gitoodo keeps across repositories (memory.sqlite in the config folder): facts, procedures, preferences and where things are found, global or per repository; list shows what applies (with --repo: global and that repository's), each with a token estimate; show prints the history of every change; texts that look like a token, key or password are refused (keep where a secret is, never the secret); entries from a worker wait as proposed Services: gitoodo service install|uninstall|start|stop [classifier|dispatcher|all] background services with the system service manager (restart on crash and reboot); default classifier; install copies this CLI to a stable per-user folder first gitoodo classifier run the classifier daemon in the foreground (what the service starts) gitoodo daemon deprecated alias of `gitoodo classifier` gitoodo dispatcher run the dispatcher in the foreground: one coding agent worker per ready issue (https://gitoodo.com/docs/dev/dispatcher/) gitoodo satellite [--stdio | --restart-idle | --drop-carried] worker machine service: runs workers for a main host (https://gitoodo.com/docs/dev/satellites/); --stdio is the SSH bridge, --restart-idle lets an idle service take up the installed build after an update, --drop-carried removes every main host's carried setup and credentials from this machine gitoodo mcp [--scope all|<account>/<owner>/<name>[#<n>]] MCP server over stdio: the ledger and the dispatcher as read tools plus change proposals that wait for the human's OK (https://gitoodo.com/docs/dev/orchestrator-chat/); --scope narrows them to one repository or item gitoodo token-purge remove every Gitoodo token from the data protection keychain (the uninstaller runs it through the service helper, which shares the app's keychain group); prints removed or unavailable Used by workers (run inside a worker session, not by hand): gitoodo ask [--issue <key>] [--check] post a question block (JSON spec on stdin) to the issue and wait for a human; `--check` only tests the spec and prints the block, nothing is posted; `gitoodo ask --help` shows the spec's fields and a complete example gitoodo worker context print compact assigned issue context as JSON; requires GITOODO_ISSUE (local workers only) gitoodo worker push | pr [--title <t>] [--body <text>] push the branch and open the pull request that closes the issue, through the account connected in Gitoodo (the worker never holds a token) gitoodo worker follow-up --title <t> --body-file <path|-> [--label <kind>] propose a follow-up issue for work outside the own issue; the dispatcher creates it with a back-reference, and a maintainer approves it before a worker picks it up gitoodo worker split --plan <path|-> split an issue too big for one run into parts (JSON plan) before writing code; the dispatcher creates them, and the issue waits until all parts are closed gitoodo worker blocked --on <#n[,#m]> --reason <text> the issue cannot go on before other issues land; the dispatcher records the dependency on the issue, ends the run, and the issue waits until they are closed gitoodo worker close --summary <text> close the issue without a pull request: an umbrella whose child issues are all closed delivered what it asks, or the issue needs no change (delivered already, obsolete); the dispatcher checks the children, or refuses while your branch or worktree changes a file, then posts the summary and closes the issue gitoodo worker needs --tool <name[,name]> --reason <text> the issue cannot be done without a command this machine lacks; the dispatcher labels it tool:<name>, ends the run, and a machine that has the command takes it gitoodo worker needs --data <path[,path]> --reason <text> the issue cannot be done without local files that cannot come to this machine; the issue goes to the main machine, which has them (never a tool: label) gitoodo worker needs --desktop <name[,name]> --reason <text> the issue needs a test desktop of this Gitoodo that this worker computer cannot reach (push your work first); the issue goes on from its branch on the main machine, which reaches every test desktop (never a tool: label) gitoodo worker input <path> copy a further local file or folder of the main machine (relative to the repository, a session transcript <id>.jsonl, or a log file of Gitoodo such as log:dispatcher.jsonl with its older generations) into the worktree gitoodo worker remember --scope global|repo --kind <kind> --text <t> [--from-answer] propose a memory entry (fact, procedure, preference, location) later runs need and cannot read from the code, never a secret; one that says the same is merged; it is used once a person approves it or workers of 3 issues proposed it gitoodo worker dispute <id> --reason <text> report memory entry <id> as wrong or outdated: it is kept, marked disputed and no longer given to workers until a person looks at it gitoodo desktop [--on NAME] <command> [args] Agent Desktop (desktop control through the accessibility tree) as Gitoodo installed it; in a worker it takes turns at the test desktop; --on reaches another machine's desktop over SSH gitoodo desktop-turn [--on NAME] "WHAT" | --done wait in line for a test desktop (prints OK, BUSY or PERSON) or give it back gitoodo hook status-line|stop|stop-failure|activity|tool-start|tool-end|needs-you Claude Code or Codex hook ping to the dispatcher (silent without one) gitoodo next --worker <id> --host <host> [--repo <owner/name>]

h: Quitting the app and the services (#737)
b: gitoodo is the headless side of Gitoodo: the classifier daemon that polls the forges of the configured accounts and a command line that asks it for the queue picture. The app does not need it and works unchanged without it. Commands gitoodo status [--changed] [--json] [--ack] gitoodo service install|uninstall gitoodo classifier gitoodo next --worker session-1 --host win [--repo owner/repo] [--account id] [--json] gitoodo done --worker session-1 --lease <id> [--result "PR ready"] [--json] gitoodo usage [--refresh] [--json] status prints one line per open issue and pull request of the covered repos, grouped like the lage picture: repo, issue#N / pr#N , status labels, age bucket, warnings, title, and a summary line at the end. Issues without status labels show [ohne Einordnung] . An account the last poll could not read (server unreachable, token missing) adds , 1 account not read to the summary line, its errors go to stderr with a hint to check address, network and token and run gitoodo doctor , and the command exits 3: an unreachable forge never looks like an empty one. --json prints the whole reply ( picture , changed , digest , polled_at , errors ); picture.summary.not_read counts the accounts not read. --changed prints nothing (unless --json ) and exits 0 when the waking lines changed since the last --ack or an issue lacks status labels, 1 otherwise. --ack stores the current state as seen. Typical wake check: gitoodo status --changed && gitoodo status --ack . usage prints the usage of each agent of the dispatcher (5-hour and weekly window, "paused until" at the limit); --refresh first has the dispatcher and every worker machine ask each agent again, as "Check limits now" in the app (at most once per 30 seconds, see docs/orchestrator/dispatcher.md , "Usage limits"). --json prints the providers. Exit code 2: the daemon is not reachable. 3: the last poll could not read an account or the configuration ( --changed still exits 0 on a change). 64: wrong usage. classifier runs the classifier daemon in the foreground; the service runs exactly this. daemon is a deprecated alias that runs the same thing and prints a note. Classifier role and read model The classifier (spec section 6) polls every repository in state observed (read only), paused and active ; repositories in state off are listed but never read. After each poll it builds a read model in memory and serves it to the app and the CLI over the local socket: request {"cmd":"read_model"} , reply {"reply":"read_model", ...} with polled_at and per repository account_id , full_name , state and the open issues, highest score first. After a start the request waits up to two minutes for the first poll; {"cmd":"read_model", "immediate":true} answers at once instead ( polled_at then is null and repos empty). The app always asks immediate and gives up after 15 s as busy , so a long first poll never keeps its views loading ( read_model_now ); per issue: number , title , html_url , labels , computed readiness ( ready , blocked , needs-clarification , needs-approval , needs-human , in-progress , in-review , stalled , held ), dependencies ( owner/repo#n ), cycle , score and the lease holder if any; readiness uses the dependency graph (open dependencies block, cycles and self-dependencies need clarification, unknown dependencies fail closed), the trust decision of section 5.3 and the label catalog; the score is the dispatcher order of section 7.1 with the weights of the score section of the orchestration config. Request {"cmd":"poll"} (reply {"reply":"poll_scheduled"} ) ends the wait between two polls; the app sends it after the user unlocked or granted a keychain token, so an account that waited for approval is read again at once. Each poll writes its errors to the activity file right before its poll record; rule notes such as "… more questions pending" go to the record's notes , never to labels_set . The types and the client ( ping , read_model , poll_now , request_at ) live in gitoodo_core::service_rpc . The classifier idles at a few MB; an integration test keeps it under 30 MB RSS without accounts. Queue writer and leases The daemon is the only Gitoodo process that writes status labels. next , done and label maintenance share one asynchronous lock, including their fresh forge reads. Run **one writer daemon per repository**; a second host must use that daemon, not start another writer for the same repository. An OS-held daemon.lock in the configuration folder prevents simultaneous writers for the same configuration, even during startup; the OS releases it after a crash. Exactly one classifier runs per configuration (#593, #600): While no service is registered, the app starts gitoodo classifier itself with its process id in GITOODO_PARENT_PID . That classifier (and a dispatcher the app starts) stops within two seconds once the app is gone (quit, crash, update), so the app leaves no orphan. On Unix the child notices that it was re-parented; on Windows, which re-parents nothing, it holds a handle on the app's process from its start and checks whether that process has ended (#1331). Once the classifier service is registered, the app starts only the service, and a classifier the app started stops by itself and hands over. The service definitions set GITOODO_SERVICE=1 . A classifier service whose lock is still held waits for it instead of exiting, so launchd or systemd do not restart it in a loop; it logs took over the classifier lock when it does. Windows: the parent watch is Unix-only for now; the app's exit stops its children there. Worker identities live inside the local OS-user trust boundary; the dispatcher ([ orchestrator/dispatcher.md ](orchestrator/dispatcher.md)) is the only component that starts workers. Enable repositories explicitly in <config>/orchestration.json (Gitoodo's own configuration): { "repos": [ { "account_id": "nas", "full_name": "owner/repo", "human": "maintainer-login", "releases": true } ], "lease_seconds": 14400, "profile": { "names": {}, "extra_labels": [] } } Missing configuration keeps the daemon read-only. Invalid configuration blocks mutations. Accounts must exist in settings.json ; disabled repositories cannot be assigned. Maintenance runs during polling for enabled repositories, including those outside the dashboard view. next --repo selects an enabled, non-disabled repository. The daemon never edits the config; the only service that does is the dispatcher, which at its start only tidies former start-mode fields and keeps halted as it was. While halted is set, next returns no assignment and the maintenance pass writes nothing ([ orchestrator/dispatcher.md ](orchestrator/dispatcher.md), "Emergency stop"). next and done are the lease commands the dispatcher works the queue with. From the command line ( gitoodo next , gitoodo done ) they never compete with it (#953): in an automation session ( GITOODO_ISSUE is automation:<id> ) both are refused with the code automation_session : an automation reports, it does not take or finish issues; for a repository whose autopilot is on (state active ), next is refused with the code autopilot_on and names the repositories: the autopilot works that queue. done from the command line does not finish a lease in such a repository either (same code). The dispatcher's own requests are not affected; the command line marks its requests with "cli": true . next returns JSON with an assignment (or null when no work is eligible). An assignment contains the full issue and its lease: id, worker, host, account, repository, issue number, expiry and completion flag. Candidates must be open, carry only ready (legacy status:bereit ), have no needs-human (the legacy name an:mensch is not recognised), stalled or extern , and either have no host restriction or a matching host: label. For --host local a host: label matches this machine's name ( orchestration.json › local_host.name , default the sanitised short host name), any of its local_host.aliases and local , without case — the same matcher as the dispatcher ( docs/orchestrator/spec.md , 7.1 item 3). Satellites match only their own configured name. A host: value that names no configured machine but a platform ( mac , win , ubu , ...; see spec 7.1) matches any host running that system. Candidates are taken in the order the app's queue shows (spec 7.1 item 4): the next release and boosted issues first, then by score (priority weight, age per hour, manual boost, release bonus, with the repository's own weights when it has them), highest first; ties go to the earlier creation time, then the lower issue number, then the configured account/repository order. Priorities are priority:p0 .. p3 (legacy prio:1..3 ); an issue without one counts as priority:p1 when it carries a bug label ( bug , typ:bug , type:bug , kind/bug , …, #1635) and as priority:p2 otherwise. A priority label always wins over the type. Changing the priority in the app. In a repository the orchestrator works on, every queued issue, every open issue of "Issues and pull requests" and an open issue's detail offer "Raise priority" and "Lower priority" (two arrows that show on hover or focus; in the detail always), and on a focused row + and - . A step swaps the priority label on the forge for the next one (the profile's name, created on the forge when missing; every other priority label goes, legacy ones included); an issue without a label starts where the dispatcher puts it ( priority:p2 , a bug priority:p1 ) and moves from there. At priority:p0 raising is off and says "Highest priority", at priority:p3 lowering. The write runs in the core ( set_issue_priority , labels::set_priority ) on every forge, reads the issue's labels fresh first and never touches other labels. The queue re-sorts at once with the new score (the repository's own weights) and goes back when the forge refuses, with the reason in a short note; afterwards the app asks the classifier to read the repositories again, so the dispatcher takes the issue in its new place from its next pick. The release view (#1707) also sets the priority of several issues at once: set_issues_priority takes the step {"to": n} per issue, which leaves exactly the profile's label for priority:p<n> (an issue that already carries only that label is left alone), one issue after the other, so a refusal stops none of the others. Dependencies are declared by a line of their own, in the body or in a comment a person wrote. The line starts (after an optional list bullet - , * , + or 1. and optional bold ** ) with one of Depends on , Blocked by , Waits for , Wartet auf , Abhängig von , Blockiert bis , Abhängigkeit(en) , Depende de or Bloqueado por (any case), an optional colon, and the references, separated by commas, spaces, and or und : Wartet auf: #12, owner/other#3 - **Depends on:** #7 and #8 #12 , repo#12 and owner/repo#12 are supported, including nested GitLab namespaces; the list ends at the first word that is no reference. Anything else is no dependency: a mention in the middle of a sentence, a closing reference, a status line such as Worker fertig: PR #1382, wartet auf gate/nas. and every comment Gitoodo wrote itself (its machine marker, see [ question-format.md ](question-format.md)). A referenced issue or pull request must be verifiably closed or merged; an open, missing or inaccessible one blocks assignment. The app's queue uses the same rule and the same lookup, so such an issue shows as blocked there, never as the queue head. When the dispatcher passes over a ready issue for open dependencies it logs dispatch.skip ( reason dependencies_open , refs the blocking references) once per issue and change, so gitoodo trace owner/repo#n explains the wait. Assignment adds in-progress before removing ready , adds the forge account's authenticated login to the assignees (people already assigned stay; GitHub adds atomically, Gitea/Forgejo and GitLab write the fresh list plus the login), then writes a gitoodo:lease v1 audit comment naming the worker an

h: Mac App Store and Microsoft Store
b: "Fragen an mich" on the phone (#1687): the desktop app serves a small web app to phones in the same local network. A phone pairs once by scanning a QR code: the phone icon in the top bar or "Pair a phone" in the status bar opens Settings → Notifications & feedback → Phone with the code already shown (#1836); once a phone is paired, the status bar shows how many and both open that page without a new pairing. After that the phone lists the questions waiting for you and answers a question card (or comments on an item without one) through the same path as the desktop's card. It can be put on the home screen and then opens like an app. Home screen (#1855): below the list a card offers to put the page on the home screen. Where the browser offers its own install prompt ( beforeinstallprompt , Chromium in a secure context) it shows an "Install" button; otherwise it names the steps for the phone's system (iPhone/iPad: Safari's Share menu, Android: the browser menu), chosen by installWay in src/mobile/model.ts . Over the plain-HTTP local address Android adds a shortcut that opens in the browser; iPhone/iPad open it full screen from the manifest ( /manifest.webmanifest , display: standalone ). The card disappears once the page runs from the home screen. Where it runs: in the desktop app ( src-tauri/src/mobile.rs ), so only while the app runs. The server and the desktop's half of the protocol are in the core ( crates/core/src/mobile/ ), the cryptography, the labels and the phone's client in crates/mobile-protocol , which the native app uses as well; the phone page is mobile.html with src/mobile/ , built into the app with the main window. Off by default: no port is open until you press "Pair a phone". The access listens while a pairing is open (10 minutes) or at least one phone is paired; unpairing the last phone, or a pairing nobody completed, closes the port again. Local network only: it listens on all IPv4 interfaces, on port 47823 when free (otherwise another free port, which it keeps), and drops connections from addresses outside the private ranges ( 10/8 , 172.16/12 , 192.168/16 ), link-local and loopback. Access on the go follows later through an end-to-end encrypted relay, with the same encryption. What the phone can do: read the questions of every account and repository the desktop shows under "Fragen an mich", answer a card (choices, yes/no, text, "explain better", a note), and post a comment on an item without a card. Like the desktop's cards (#1876) it can also close the issue (an optional reason is posted first, after a short confirmation), put an item off until later (1 hour, tomorrow morning, 1 week; the desktop's "Later") and, on a task, tick its checklist and mark it done (optionally closing the issue) or hand it back to the orchestrator with a note. A closed or finished item leaves the desktop list at once and the phone list with its next check; the window says "Closed on <phone>", "Done on <phone>" or "Handed back … on <phone>". A refused close names the reason (no right to close, open prerequisites on the forge). The comment that finishes a task uses the desktop's words in the phone's language. Since #1895 it can also list the repositories with their autopilot, switch the autopilot of one on or to paused, and look at its running and latest sessions (see "Orchestrator" under "Protocol"). Nothing else: no settings, no tokens, no transcripts. Desktop only, on purpose: forwarding a question to someone else (it picks people from the forge and lets the local AI draft the note), trusting a contribution's author (an app-wide security setting), the AI answer assist and bringing back a snoozed item (the phone does not list snoozed items). Same list as the desktop (#1839): the core leaves out what the desktop list leaves out (switched-off repos, snoozed items, items answered in the app) and gives every item its place ( ListPlace in crates/core/src/sync/counts.rs ): question for the list, approval for the approvals' bundle, other for repos without the autopilot, which the phone folds away and does not count, like the desktop's "N more". The page's title carries the same count as the tray. No notifications yet: the page is served over plain HTTP on a local address, which is no secure context. Phone browsers offer notifications, push, service workers and the home-screen badge only in a secure context: Android (Chrome and others) needs HTTPS for all of them, and iPhone/iPad (iOS 16.4 and later) needs HTTPS and the page added to the home screen. So the phone only refreshes while it is open (see "Answered once" below) and when it comes to the front. Notifications arrive with the encrypted relay, which serves the page over HTTPS and can send Web Push. Answered once A question is answered once, whichever client answers it (#1873). The phone's answer is posted by the desktop app through the same path as the window's card ( answer_card in src-tauri/src/answer.rs ), so the core sees every answer: Desktop at once: every step of an answer from any client (sending, answered, failed) goes to every window as the answered event with the item, the core's mark after the step and where the answer came from ( AnsweredBy : computer , phone with the phone's name, forge ). The window's answer marks ( src/state/answered.tsx , answerMarks.ts ) follow it, so a phone's answer hides the question in the desktop list the moment it is sent, the window says "Answered on <phone>", and a failed post brings it back with "The answer from <phone> was not sent". A window that opens later reads the marks with get_answer_marks . Phone within seconds: the open page asks every 3 seconds with the sync call whether the list changed. The reply carries the list's version, a fingerprint of exactly the list the phone would get ( list_version in crates/core/src/mobile/mod.rs ), and the list itself only when the phone's version differs; an unchanged check is a few bytes. Every change counts without bookkeeping: a poll, an answer from any client, a failed post, a snooze running out, a repo switched off. An answer on the desktop therefore leaves the phone's list within about 3 seconds. An open question the desktop no longer lists says "This question is no longer open" and offers no sending. Checks only run while the page is in the front; no new port, service or relay. No second answer: one answer per item runs at a time ( ItemLocks in crates/core/src/answer_lock.rs ); a second one waits, then is refused while the first one's mark covers the question. Right before posting, the core reads the issue's comments once and refuses when the account already answered this block in the marker format (another computer, the browser). The refused client is told already_answered and where: the window says "Already answered on <phone>" (or "in Gitoodo on this computer", or "the answer is already in the issue"), the phone "Already answered on <computer>" and so on, and its card goes away. A post that fails takes the mark back on every client, so the question can be answered again. Protocol A browser on a local address gets no trusted HTTPS, so every request is encrypted end to end instead. Base64url without padding throughout; labels are ASCII. Pairing offer (QR code). http://<ip>:<port>/#pair=<base64url(json)> with {"v":3,"m":1,"k":<desktop public key>,"t":<token>,"x":<expiry, unix seconds>} ( v the desktop's protocol version, m the oldest phone version it serves; see "Compatibility"). k is a fresh X25519 key for this one pairing, t 16 random bytes. The part after # never reaches a server; the page removes it from the address and the history at once. Pairing request. The phone makes its own X25519 key p and computes proof = HMAC-SHA256(t, "gitoodo-mobile-v1 pair proof" || p) key = HKDF-SHA256(ikm = X25519(phone, k), salt = t, info = "gitoodo-mobile-v1 device key" || p || k) , 32 bytes and sends POST /api/pair {"v":<agreed version>,"m":<its oldest>,"p":…,"h":proof,"c":seal(key, "gitoodo-mobile-v1 pair", {"name","ts"})} . The desktop checks the proof first (a request without the token leaves the pairing open), then derives the same key (the pairing's private key is used up by this), opens the hello, checks its time, stores the device and answers {"c":seal(key, "gitoodo-mobile-v1 paired", {"device","host"})} . Calls. POST /api/call {"v":<agreed version>,"m":<its oldest>,"d":<device id>,"c":seal(key, "gitoodo-mobile-v1 call <id>", call)} with call = {"id":<16 random bytes>,"ts":<unix ms>,"op":…,"args":…} ; ops are sync ( since : the list version the phone shows, or null ; replies {"version","items","protocol","caps"} , items left out when the version is since , protocol the desktop's {"version","min"} and caps its capabilities, see "Compatibility"), questions (the plain list without a version), answer ( account , repo , number , kind , block , answers , note ), comment ( account , repo , number , kind , body ), and since #1876 close (the item and reason ), finish (the item, finish : {"done":{"close":…}} or "hand_back" , lead , note , label ), tick (the item, index , text , checked ; replies the new checklist) and snooze ( account , repo , number , until in unix seconds). Each one runs through the same path as the desktop's command ( close_card , finish_card , tick_card in src-tauri/src/answer.rs , the hub's snooze), under the same per-item lock as answers. The reply is {"c":seal(key, "gitoodo-mobile-v1 reply <id>", {"re":<call id>,"ok",…})} ; the phone accepts only a reply that names its call. A refused call carries "ok":false and the category in error ; already_answered adds "data":{"by":{"via":"computer"|"phone"|"forge","name":…}} ( name only for a phone). An op the desktop does not know is refused for that call alone with unsupported . Orchestrator (#1895). Three ops let a paired phone see the orchestrator and steer it per repository, built from the same sources as the window's sidebar and worker list ( crates/core/src/mobile/orchestrator.rs , the app side in src-tauri/src/mobile.rs ): repos (no args) replies {"orchestrator","dispatcher","repos":[…]} : orchestrator is false in direct mode (then repos is empty), dispatcher whether the dispatcher answered. Each repo is {"account","repo","state","autopilot","running","waiting","stalled","poll_failed"} with state active , paused or observed (the stored state of orchestration.json first, as the window's switch); a repo switched off in the settings is not listed. sessions ( account , repo ) replies {"account","repo","state","running":[…],"recent":[…]} . A session is {"number","title","state","since","secs","host","hint"} : state is working , needs_you , at_prompt , held , limited or disk_paused for a running worker and in_review , needs_human or stalled for the latest ones (at most 10); since and secs are unix seconds and the running time, hint a code ( {"kind":"stall","cause","runs"} , {"kind":"pull","number"} , {"kind":"limit","until"} ). No transcript, no comment text, no token. autopilot ( account , repo , on ) takes the window's step: active → paused ( on: false ), paused → active , observed → active with backlog ask as the switch adopts a repo, anything else unchanged. It writes through the same store paths as set_repo_state and adopt_repo ( src-tauri/src/labels.rs ), sets an activated repo up on the forge in the background like the window ( prepare_repo ), and replies {"state","autopilot"} . The window gets the repo-steered event with the phone's name, reads the states again and says "Autopilot paused for <repo> on <phone>" (or "switched on"). Refusals of these ops: unknown_repo (an account that is not connected or a repository the desktop does not list), no_right (a repository switched off in the settings, which the phone may neither see nor change), direct_mode (no orchestrator); a failed write carries the desktop command's category ( store ). sync adds "orchestrator":<version> in orchestrator mode, a fingerprint of what repos and every repo's sessions show without the running times ( orch

h: Per mode: orchestrator, working directly, answering
When a new version needs more
b: Gitoodo needs a personal access token per account. The token wizard (Settings > Accounts > add) and the Replace token … dialog of a stored account name the permissions in the words of the forge's own token page, with the reason for each. This page is the same list for later. The wizard texts live in src/views/settings/permissionGuide.ts ; tests/token-permissions.test.ts fails when this page, the wizard and the checks in crates/core/src/forge drift apart. GitHub Classic token (Settings > Developer settings > Personal access tokens (classic)); the wizard opens the page with both boxes ticked: Permission Why repo Read repositories and issues, send answers as comments, close issues read:user Recognise which account the token belongs to Fine-grained token: choose the repositories under "Repository access" and set under "Repository permissions": Permission Why Metadata: Read-only List repositories (GitHub grants this automatically) Issues: Read and write Read issues, send answers as comments, close issues GitLab Permission Why api Read issues, send answers as comments, close issues read_api is enough for reading only; without api Gitoodo cannot answer. Forgejo and Gitea Forgejo and Gitea cannot preselect permissions by link. Set them by hand on the opened page (User settings > Applications): pick this access level for each category and leave all others on "No access". Category Access level Why user Read Recognise which account the token belongs to repository Read List the repositories of the account issue Read and write Read issues, send answers as comments, close issues Per mode: orchestrator, working directly, answering The lists above are what answering questions needs. The wizard asks what Gitoodo should do with the repositories, preselects the operating mode chosen in onboarding (or set in the app) and shows one merged list for that mode: each category once, the highest access level wins, plus the role the account needs in the repository. It goes on only after I have set these permissions on the token is ticked; switching to a mode that needs more asks again. The rights per mode come from crates/core/src/forge/rights.rs , the merge from src/views/settings/tokenBlock.ts . Forge Working directly Orchestrator, in addition Forgejo / Gitea repository : Read and write organization : Read and write, only to create or delete repositories in organisations GitHub classic — delete_repo , only to create or delete repositories GitHub fine-grained Contents: Read and write Pull requests, Administration, Commit statuses: Read and write (Administration also creates and deletes) GitLab — — ( api covers creating and deleting) Role in the repository Write (GitLab: Developer) Admin (GitLab: Maintainer), for repository settings such as merge styles and branch protection The organisation scope is optional (#978): Forgejo and Gitea refuse creating and deleting a repository that belongs to an organisation without write:organization , even when the token has write:repository ; GitHub classic tokens delete only with delete_repo . A token without it is still stored and works on every repository; the account in the settings names the gap ("Only to create or delete repos") with Replace token … , and the removal dialog names the scope before the delete is confirmed. A separate orchestrator (worker) account per forge host (#764, docs/orchestrator/spec.md 5.3.1) needs the orchestrator's rights without repository settings ( forge::rights::worker_rights ): no Administration permission and no admin role; write access (GitLab: Developer, Maintainer to merge into protected branches) is enough. Repository settings stay with the user's own account. Creating the worker account automatically ( docs/orchestrator/setup.md , "Automatic worker account") needs more on the own account, only for that moment: Forgejo/Gitea a site administrator whose token has write:admin ; GitLab self-managed an administrator token with api (and Admin Mode where the instance enforces it). Without them the step falls back to the guide; the own token is never asked to gain these scopes for anything else. The worker token it creates has exactly read:user , write:repository , write:issue (Forgejo/Gitea) or api with a 364-day expiry (GitLab). How the check finds out GitHub classic tokens list their scopes in a header and GitLab tokens on /personal_access_tokens/self . Forgejo and Gitea reveal nothing: reading scopes are probed with cheap reads, and the write scopes beyond answering ( write:repository , write:organization ) with a write the forge refuses: an empty body to POST /api/v1/repos/migrate and POST /api/v1/orgs . The forge checks the token's scopes before it reads the body, so a missing scope answers 403 with its name and a present one a validation error; nothing is ever created. Only a named scope counts as missing, so an older forge without scoped tokens reports nothing. GitHub fine-grained tokens reveal no permissions; there the forge names a missing one at the action. The wizard stores a token only when it gives everything the chosen mode needs (writing for working directly and the orchestrator); a token without the optional organisation scope is stored and the gap stays visible on the account. When a new version needs more The check runs when an account is added, its token replaced and synced, and again whenever the accounts in the settings open. If the stored token lacks a permission, the account shows what is missing and offers Replace token … . Replacing a token Replace token … sits on every account in Settings > Accounts (the key icon while the token is fine, a button while it is rejected, missing or short of permissions), on the scope hint and the sync error bar, in the repository rights check, the removal dialog, the status page and the worker account section. It opens a small dialog, not the wizard: one masked paste field (with Show ), a Create token on <host> link (GitHub and GitLab preselect the scopes; Forgejo and Gitea cannot) and the folded permission list. Save sends the token to the core, which: trims it and checks it against the forge; a network or forge error stores nothing; refuses a token of another user (logins compared case-insensitively) and names both logins; reads the scopes: a token without a scope the sync needs is refused, because the account would stop working; a token that only lacks scopes for answering or working is stored after Save anyway (Forgejo tokens cannot be edited later, a partial token beats a revoked one, and the account keeps the gap marked); missing scopes for creating or deleting repositories never stop it; stores it under the same keychain entry. If the write fails halfway, the old token is written back. Nothing is stored before steps 1 to 3 have passed. Afterwards the account's token error and banners clear, its sync restarts, the scope marks and the open rights checks run again. The account keeps its id and every setting; all repositories of the account use the new token, since they share the one keychain entry. The background services (classifier, dispatcher) read the token from the keychain on every cycle, so they use the new token from their next cycle without a restart. On macOS the app then grants the service helper access to the rewritten item where needed (restarting the services only if a grant changed something) and asks the classifier to poll now; on Windows the scheduled task reads the Credential Manager on its next cycle. A token handed to a headless service as GITOODO_TOKEN_<ID> or a systemd credential ( docs/daemon.md ) overrides the keychain and is replaced where it was set. Release rule: a version that adds a required permission lists it in the changelog under "Added" or "Changed" as "New permission required: ...", and the permission appears in the lists above. Closing can also be refused even with write permission: HTTP 412 means forge prerequisites are unmet, for example open issue dependencies. Gitoodo explains this and points to the issue in the browser; it does not remove dependencies or report the issue as closed.

t: States: what Gitoodo shows and what you do about it
h: New and removed repositories on the forge
2. Issue: where a piece of work stands
3. Worker: one agent on one issue
4. Things Gitoodo repairs on its own
b: Gitoodo is an orchestrator: it takes issues from your forges, hands them to AI coding workers and brings their results back as pull requests. This page is the one map of that flow. Every mark in the sidebar, every session tile, every column in "All repos" and every line on the status page belongs to one of the states below, and each state says whether anything is asked of you (#870). The short version: you act only on "needs you" and "stuck" , and on "in review" when your merge setting leaves the merge to you. Everything else moves by itself: failing checks go back to the worker, and anything left behind is cleaned up by Gitoodo, not by you. 1. Repository: autopilot on or paused Every repository has one switch (#877), in the sidebar and in the settings. State Gitoodo reads Sets labels Starts workers What it means Autopilot on yes yes yes Gitoodo works the repository's issues Paused yes yes¹ no no new worker starts; questions fold away² ¹ Only in a repository the autopilot worked before; one it never worked stays untouched. ² Still in "Asked of me", folded behind "N more from repos without autopilot – show" (below). "Asked of me" and every counter (header, sidebar, tray, notifications) list what waits for you in repositories with the autopilot on (#897). What waits in paused repositories or in repositories without the autopilot stays behind "N more from repos without autopilot – show" at the end of the list; Settings → Notifications → "Questions from repos without autopilot too" shows it for good. Direct mode always lists every repository. A repository you never want to see is removed from the sidebar ("Remove"); "Show again" in the settings brings it back. Pausing a repository starts no new worker there; workers already running finish their issue normally (nothing is stopped, the in-progress label stays until they are done). The message after the switch says so and names where the repository's questions now are: in "Asked of me" under "N more from repos without autopilot". The settings hint and the guide say the same. New and removed repositories on the forge The repository list of an account follows the forge. Gitoodo lists every repository the token can see (own repositories, collaborations and those of its organisations, every page): on every poll of the account (the sync interval, with the sync's backoff after errors); with the sync button in the header; when the window opens, reloads or gains focus, for accounts not listed within the last minute; each time Settings → Repos or a view's repository selection opens. A repository created on the forge appears with the next listing, everywhere at once (sidebar, filters, Settings → Repos), with the state of every new repository: paused, nothing is written to it. Once a sync is through, the header says what it found ("1 new repo"). A repository the forge no longer lists (deleted, renamed, or the token lost access) keeps its settings: Settings → Repos shows it below the list as "No longer on the forge" until you remove it there. A listing that fails changes nothing, so a passing error never drops a repository. 2. Issue: where a piece of work stands The labels on the forge are the source of truth; the classifier sets them, the dispatcher reads them. A repository row in the sidebar shows at most two marks (#740): the rotating circle in front of its name while a worker runs there, and after its name the "needs you" mark, only while something needs you there (a question or approval, or a stuck issue), with the count when there are several. Everything the autopilot handles by itself gets no mark on the row. The "needs you" mark is a button: with one waiting question it opens that question, otherwise "Asked of me", which lists stuck issues and machine waits with their ways out (#919); the row's menu offers the same as "Open what needs you". A folded group or owner sums its repositories the same way. Hovering the row says, line by line: the repository and its switch; what goes on now, each with its number ("4 workers running · 2 in review"); then each thing that needs you with what to do; then at most one quiet line for the queue ("52 queued", ready and blocked issues together). The screen reader hears the same words. Opening a repository lists up to three lines of current work under it, the running ones first, each with its own mark from the table below. Its filter "Only with open questions or work" keeps the repositories with a question waiting for you, a stuck issue, or a worker running or starting (here or on another machine); blocked, ready, in-review or finished issues and running checks alone do not count (#948). A repository listed twice (under Favourites and in its group) is marked once, in the row it was opened from. Mark Meaning What you do rotating circle Working : a worker is on it right now nothing filled circle with "?" Needs you : a question or an approval answer it on the forge or in Gitoodo; work goes on filled circle with "?" Stuck ( stalled ): the autopilot gave up on it choose a way out on "Asked of me" (see below) filled circle with "?" Stuck on a machine only you can provide choose a way out on "Asked of me" (see below) triangle with "!" Checks fail on the pull request nothing: the worker gets it back to fix them diamond In review : a pull request waits review and merge (or let Gitoodo merge, see settings) circle with a bar Blocked by a dependency or a missing machine nothing: it resolves by itself circle with a dot Claimed by a worker on another machine nothing dashed circle Ready : starts when a worker slot is free nothing check mark Done : a worker just finished nothing Only the two "?" states put a mark on the repository row; the others show in the issue lines under an opened repository, and hovering a line explains it in one sentence. Each issue line is an entry of the sidebar tree of its own: a click, or Enter and Space with the keyboard, opens the page that belongs to it, and the line stays marked while that page shows. The arrows walk repositories and their lines together, Left goes back to the repository. Line Opens Working the repository with that worker's session large (else the issue) Needs you the question's card, where it is answered Stuck "Asked of me", with the line's ways out Checks fail, Blocked, Done the issue's sheet on the repository page "+n more" the repository page with its issue list in view Three lines show under a repository; a fourth shows itself instead of "+1 more". An issue the repository page has not loaded opens by its number and is read from the forge. With an issue's details open, one click on a line opens it. Back returns to the page before, in the narrow layout with the focus on the line. The repository page's list "Issues and pull requests" shows the open work; its header number counts open items only. The chips under the search narrow it by state, and the last chip, "Done" with its count, adds closed issues and merged or closed pull requests: muted, with a check (issue), a merge mark (merged pull request) or a cross (closed unmerged) and when it happened ("done 2 days ago", "merged …", "closed …"), after the open work in every sort. A search without chips covers open and done items alike. Done items are read from the forge one page of 50 at a time: the first page once per visit of the repository (for the count and the search), further pages with "Load more done items", never on the sync's refreshes. When an open item leaves the list, the first page is read once more, so it shows up as done. The count comes from the forge (on GitHub its search, on GitLab the list's total); where the forge gives none it reads "50+ done". An issue is stuck when its worker made no progress after several restarts, or its checks still fail after the last restart. An issue stalled only because its machine could not start a worker goes back to ready by itself. Before a stuck issue reaches "Asked of me" as a question, the resolver tries it once ( docs/orchestrator/resolver.md ): a run of a coding agent ahead of new issues that finds the cause, fixes it and goes on with the branch. While it waits or runs, the line says "The resolver takes it next – …" or "The resolver is on it with <agent> – …" and offers no ways out, and its worker tile is marked "Resolver". When it got the issue moving, stalled goes and the issue is ready again with a short note; when it could not, the issue gets a question with the cause, what was tried and how to go on ( needs-human ). A sign-in only you can make is asked at once, without a run. The resolver never touches extern issues, issues with your own session or an open question, or paused and hidden repositories, and it is switched off in Settings → Dispatcher or per repository. "Asked of me" lists every stuck issue (#919). A line shows only the reason in a few words and one button, Solve ; it opens the ways out that fit the cause, the recommended one first and marked, each with one quiet line saying what it does: Reason shown Recorded cause Ways out (recommended first) "The worker hung" hung Solve with an agent, View issue, Pause "3 runs without a result" no_result Solve with an agent, View issue, Pause "Checks keep failing" checks_failing Solve with an agent, View issue, Pause "Merging keeps failing" merge_failed Solve with an agent, View issue, Pause "Conflicts with the base branch" conflict Solve with an agent, View issue, Pause "The branch could not be updated" update_failed Solve with an agent, View issue, Pause "A required check (gate/nas) was never reported …" checks_missing Solve with an agent, View issue, Pause "The autopilot got no further" unknown , none Solve with an agent, View issue, Pause "Working copy was in use" lease_refused Try again (passing), Solve with an agent, … "The base branch moved faster than the checks ran" base_moving Try again (passing), Solve with an agent, … "The agent waited for a sign-in" login_prompt Try again (after signing in), Solve with an agent, … "The agent waited for a confirmation at its start" trust_prompt see below Try again puts the issue back into the queue ( ready , the stalled label goes). It is offered only where another run can go differently, and says why: the cause was passing (a held working copy, a base branch that moved on), it is gone once the agent is signed in again, or an update fixed it. The only cause an update fixed so far is the confirmation at the agent's start (Claude Code and Codex no longer wait for the folder trust prompt since 2026-11-17): a trust_prompt stall from before that offers "Try again" (an update since fixed it) when this app is newer than the fix; otherwise it gets the ways of the other causes. Every other cause repeats, and another run would only spend tokens. The cause decides, not the recorded transient flag (older records call a hang passing). Solve with an agent opens a session of your own ( docs/agent-session.md , "Solve with an agent") in the issue's worktree, with the issue, the cause and the end of the last run as its first message. The issue keeps stalled meanwhile, so the autopilot never takes it. While the session runs, the line says so and offers "Open session". Once it ended, the line offers **Hand back to the autopilot** in one click ( ready ; the next worker goes on from the branch, and the ended session's tile closes); "Solve" keeps the other ways. Pause the autopilot here takes the issue out of the queue: its status goes and extern comes, and the autopilot no longer touches it. To undo it, remove extern on the forge. It replaces "Put back" and is the one way to dismiss an issue without solving it. View issue opens it in its repository. With two or more stuck issues that may be tried again, Try N again above the list tries exactly those (never the ones whose cause repeats), and its hint names why. After a way out the line goes and every count drops at once, before the next poll shows the change. The dispatcher records the cause in stall.json (state folder) when it gives u

t: "All repos": pages and where things went
b: "All repos" is the second entry of the navigation, after "Overview". In orchestrator mode it has three pages (#933): Page What it holds Sessions The running sessions of every repository as tiles, the queue, workers on other machines and orphaned issues. The default page. Issues Every issue and pull request, grouped by repository, with search, filters and the quick filters; the row actions (terminal, pause, restart, boost, hold or veto). Release The release status per repository (unchanged). Direct mode keeps In progress (its default), Issues and Pull requests. The statistics ("Overview": throughput with its trend, utilisation, the activity of twelve weeks and achievements, docs/metrics.md , "Overview dashboard") are no page of "All repos" any more: they are the app's start page ( docs/startup.md , "Where the window opens"). The app opens on it, and the navigation's first entry, "Overview" (or the Gitoodo wordmark in the header), leads back to it from anywhere. Its tiles lead on: "Worker slots" to Sessions, "Queued" and "Active repos" to Issues, "Failing checks" to Issues with that quick filter. Done issues (#1458) Each repository on Issues ends with the group "Done", collapsed by default: its recently closed issues, newest close first, with the closing date, "not planned" where the forge records why (GitHub; Forgejo, Gitea and GitLab do not), and the merged pull request that closed it ( Closes #12 in its description). The app reads them only when the group opens, one forge page (50 closed issues and pull requests) at a time; "Load more" reads the next. The classifier's poll never reads closed issues. The Rust core keeps the pages per repository for five minutes ( crates/core/src/done.rs ); when the forge cannot be reached later, the older copy shows with a note. An issue reopened since disappears as soon as the read model lists it as open. The quick filter "Done" counts the issues closed this week, from the same activity as the overview's "Closed, week"; a click shows just those, across the repositories in scope. Search and label filters leave done issues out unless "incl. done" (next to the filters, shown while searching) is on; readiness, failing checks and held merges concern open issues only. Where did it go Before #933 orchestrator mode also had "In progress", "Activity" and "Control", and the overview listed what needed the user. Nothing of them was dropped without a new place: Before Now In progress: run line (running, paused, not reachable) The header's overall state and "Stop all"; the status page names the stopped part. In progress: running workers with Terminal, "Left behind" Sessions (tiles, terminal, "Orphaned"). In progress: pull requests ready to merge Issues, "In review" group of each repository. In progress: up next Issues, quick filter "Up next"; the queue on Sessions. In progress: stuck (blocked, stalled, held, needs a human) Issues, quick filters "Blocked", "Stalled" and "Held merges"; questions and approvals on "Asked of me". Control: pause switch "Orchestrator on/off" "Stop all" in the header (also its keyboard shortcut); both always set the same switch. Control: merge control (held and vetoed pull requests, by number) "Control merge" on the pull request's row under Issues; quick filter "Held merges" lists them all with "Release". Control: pause single repositories The autopilot switch of the repository in the sidebar and in its settings. Control: leftovers with unsaved work Settings › Storage, section "Leftovers" (only while there are any). Control: why a ready issue waits for a worker machine Status page, on the line of the affected part, with the same steps (name this computer, show the labels). Control: "Clean up now" while the disk is low Status page, on the workers' line next to the low-disk note. Control: token problems Every page of "All repos" (only while there is a problem), and the status page. Activity: the log of every write to the forge Status page, "Activity", collapsed and loaded on demand. Overview: "Needs you" list and questions tile The header's count and "Asked of me". Overview: failing checks list Overview tile "Failing checks" (the rate), which opens Issues with the quick filter "Failing checks". Overview: work in flight Sessions. Overview: the statistics page of "All repos" The start page, the navigation's first entry "Overview" (the header's wordmark leads there too). A saved last view or a deep link to a removed page opens its new place: "Control" opens Issues, "Activity" the default page ( legacyBoardPage in src/state/lastView.ts ). A saved "Overview" opens the start page, and "All repos" then opens on its default page. The help topics "All repos", "Overview", "Merge control" and "Status" and the site docs say the same.

h: 5.2 Manually set labels (not by the worker account)
15. Migration plan (proposal; each step mergeable, the system stays usable in between)
b: Status: agreed design, ready for implementation planning (2026-11-12). Source: design interview with the maintainer on the planning whiteboard. This file is the single source of truth for the orchestrator; where it contradicts older docs ( docs/daemon.md , docs/status-model.md , the former integration doc of the external orchestrator, docs/question-format.md ), this file wins and those docs are to be updated. Values marked (default) are configurable. Items marked (proposal) were not decided in detail by the maintainer and may be refined by the implementer; flag deviations in the PR description. 1.
