h: Dependencies join the release (#1824, before: pulled-in issues, #1530)
Completing a release and its automations (#1145)
Release view: completing, runs, settings and sessions (#1146)
b: Mental model, as the app says it: a release is one goal per repository: which issues have to be in before you publish. Gitoodo works on release issues first. Using releases The board tab "Release" shows every repository with release planning on as a tree: below each repository its open releases, the next one first, and last "Ohne Release" with its open issues in no release, so every open issue of the repository is found below it (see "Release tree" under "App"). A short walk through it: Plan. "Neues Release" on a repository row creates a release, a milestone named with a version (the dialog suggests the next one). The flag on a board row or "Ändern" in the issue sheet puts an issue into the next release, a later one or none. Without any release, the empty state offers both: add issues to the next release, or create a release with a version. Let the autopilot work. Issues of the next release go first in the queue, and the issues they depend on with them. Nothing else changes; the rest of the queue runs as before. Set it up once (gear "Release-Einstellungen" on the repository row, always shown): pick a template and "Übernehmen", then adjust the tabs. Versionierung decides the version suggestion, Zuordnung the rules that put issues into a release or suggest them, Abschluss the steps that run when you complete a release, Sitzung the task of the release session. Every change saves by itself, like the other repository settings (#926); a part with problems stays unsaved and says so. Prepare ("Release-Sitzung …" in the release's "…"): a release session gives a coding agent or a plain terminal the version, the issues and the notes, in the working copy or a fresh worktree. Complete ("Release abschließen", a ticked circle, once every issue is done): the dialog shows the plan first, where open issues go and every step, the irreversible ones marked, and nothing runs before you confirm. A token that lacks a right the steps need refuses the plan before anything is written. A failed step can be retried or skipped from the run row. "Danach" decides what the autopilot does once the release is closed: "Autopilot anhalten" (the default) pauses it, and the tree then offers "Mit 1.6.0 starten"; "Gleich mit 1.6.0 weitermachen" lets it go straight on with the next release. The help center has a topic "Releases" of its own (the release page's help link opens it). Command steps run your own scripts in the local checkout of the repository. The templates point at ./scripts/release/*.sh , which the repository provides; until it does, the step fails with the script's error and nothing else happens. A minimal skeleton: #!/bin/sh # scripts/release/upload.sh: upload the build of this release. set -eu echo "Uploading ${GITOODO_RELEASE_TAG} of ${GITOODO_REPO}" # The notes are in "$GITOODO_RELEASE_NOTES_FILE", the issues as JSON in "$GITOODO_RELEASE_ISSUES". # Exit 0 when done; any other exit fails the step and shows the last lines of the output. A step gets no token; a script that needs one reads it from the system's own secret store. A version script (scheme "Eigenes Skript") prints the next version and gets GITOODO_LAST_VERSION , GITOODO_VERSION_RAISE and the release's issues (see "Own script" below). Scope Per repository, an issue belongs to the next release when it is in the next release milestone (see "Queue order"), open or closed (reason milestone ), it carries release:next (reason label ), or it is a dependency, recursively, of a member (reason dependency ). Only dependencies inside the same repository count. A closed issue stays in only through the milestone, the label or as a dependency, so a finished dependency stays part of the release. While no release milestone is open, release:next alone is the next release. Dependencies join the release (#1824, before: pulled-in issues, #1530) The sub-tasks and blockers of an issue are needed for it, so they join its release on their own; nobody has to add them by hand. A dependency is what the release view shows as one: a dependency line ( Depends on #12 , Wartet auf: #12 , …) in the issue's body or in a person's comment, the forge's own dependencies, and the open parts of a split issue (#2061; only parts Gitoodo's own accounts opened, the same rule as for the parent's wait). A split gives each new part the parent's milestone and release:next at once; a part without one (split before, or the write failed) joins in the hygiene's next pass. When an issue goes into a release (the add dialog, "+", "Change release …", the chat), its open dependencies in the same repository go with it in the same operation, transitively. The add dialog says so before saving ("+ 3 dependencies (sub-tasks and blockers) come along") and marks each one on its row. After saving, the release view shows them at once, already below the issue that needs them (the same rule as the report's, among the added issues); the next poll confirms the place and may move one below a member that was in the release before. The hygiene pass adds dependencies that appear later: for every open issue in an open release, its open dependencies join that release, the earliest release first. Each join is logged ( release.dependency_joined ) and named in the classifier's activity ("#12 joined v1.4 as a dependency of #10"). These writes count towards the pass's limit of release writes. Without the milestone rule the pass only writes release:next ; a dependency of a release milestone then joins when its issue is put into the release in the app. Where a dependency already is decides: in the same release or an earlier one it stays (the earlier release ships it first anyway); in no release it joins. In a later release it is pulled forward into the release that needs it (the activity says so: "pulled forward from v1.5") only when a pass of Gitoodo put it there (a rule or an earlier join, kept as placed in release-rules.json while the issue is still there). One a person put into a later release, in the app or on the forge, stays where they put it (#2061): the hygiene never undoes a person's release choice. Its release then waits for it ("Out of order" below), and the focus never starts it for the earlier release; moving one of the two in the app resolves it. Putting an issue into a release in the app ("Change release …") is the person's own choice and takes its dependencies along from a later release too. Moving an issue into a later release takes the issues that wait for it along (#2046). An issue in an earlier release that waits for the moved one (directly or over another such issue) could not be done before it, so its release could not ship either; it goes into the same later release in the same operation. "Change release …" says so before saving ("+ 2 issues waiting for it go along: #154, #300"), and each move is logged ( release.dependent_followed ). Issues already in that release or a later one, and issues in no release, stay where they are. The order stays visible. Every row says what it waits for ("waits for #249, #2160"); a blocker that is planned in a later release or in none is named in red below it ("Out of order: #2160 is planned later or in no release"), so a split that came from the forge, a removal by hand or an older build is seen at once. Taking an issue out of every release while issues in a release wait for it says so in "Change release …" before saving; they stay. Closed dependencies are done and are ignored. Another repository: a dependency there never joins (each repository plans its own releases). It is listed under its member ("belongs to #44 · other repo (owner/lib) · not in the release"), does not count, and while it is open it still holds the release's completion. A removal by hand sticks: a dependency a person takes out of the release stays out while its issue still needs it, like for the assignment rules. It is then listed under its member as "belongs to #44 · not in the release" and holds the completion while open. The counts name what they leave out. The release's summary line counts members only ("2 open · 1 in progress") and adds the open items it lists without counting them ("+1 not in the release"), so the rows and the numbers add up. Taking an issue out keeps its dependencies. Gitoodo has no reliable record of whether a person also wanted a dependency in the release on its own (it may have been added by hand before, or be needed by another issue), so it leaves them where they are; take them out by hand if they should go too. Dependencies that joined are members like every other issue: they count in the progress ( 3/5 , "1 open · 1 in progress"), the same as the forge's milestone. The release view lists every item below the item of the same release that needs it ( via : the first item, by number, at the top of its dependency chain), one level indented; a later release does the same. Every issue that is a member gets a release chip (flag and version) on its rows: the Issues list of a repository, the board of all repositories and the detail sheet. Its milestone is the one source; a label or a pulled-in issue never makes a chip. The chip opens the release view at that release (a later one opened too). The row's release choice then reads "Change release …". Open priority:p0 issues used to be members by themselves (reason priority ), without anything on the forge. Since #1143 the assignment rule "Urgent issues join the next release" (on by default, see "Assignment rules") writes them into the next release instead, so they are visible on the forge and a person can take them out again. The reason priority is no longer sent. Gitoodo writes only release:next . It reads the legacy release:muss as release:next and release:später as "not in the next release" (it adds nothing); neither is ever written. Adding an issue through the app removes a legacy later label from it. Planning is switched per repository in the settings, right beside the repository's activation ("Release planning", default on; stored as releases in the repository options). With it off, the repository has no scope, no bonus and does not appear in the views. Labels and milestones A repository plans its releases as milestones: **a milestone whose title is a version is a release**, and release:next stands for "the next release, version not decided yet". Other milestones (sprints, themes) stay the user's own and are never treated as releases. Several open release milestones are a normal state: the next one is picked as in "Queue order", the others are later releases (see "Releases by hand"). Membership is the milestone. release:next only marks issues for the next release while it has no version; as soon as a release milestone becomes the next release (created in the app, on the forge or by the user's answer to the milestone question), the hygiene moves every open release:next issue without a milestone into it and takes the label off ( hygiene::takes_over ). This also carries data from before the milestone model over without a migration step: an existing release:next issue keeps counting as the next release and moves into the milestone on the first poll after it exists. It uses only the forge adapter's milestone and label calls, so it works the same on Forgejo/Gitea, GitHub and GitLab (the calls per forge: crates/core/tests/release_forge.rs ). The forge calls behind it came with step 1 of epic #1139 (#1140); the app shows all of it since #1148. A milestone title counts as a release version ( forge::release::release_version ) when, after trimming, it is optionally v / V directly before the number, or one of the words version , release , build , ver (any case) followed by a space, - or _ , then one to four numbers separated by dots (each at most nine digits), then optionally a pre-release or build part after - or + of letters, digits, dots and hyphens ( -rc.1 , +20261119 ), allowed only after a dotted number or a prefix word, and nothing else. So v1.2.3 , 1.2 , 2026.11 , 42 , build 42 , Release 1.4 and 1.0.0-rc.1 are releases; Spri

Every open issue in the overview has exactly one status. Code: crates/core/src/status.rs . Statuses and recommended labels Status Standard label Derived when open status/open nothing else applies in_progress status/in-progress the issue has an assignee in_review status/in-review an open pull request closes it ( Closes #N ) blocked status/blocked never derived, label only needs_user status/needs-you an open question to the user exists Standard labels match case-insensitively. Precedence Label mapping of the account (label name to status). Standard labels from the table. Derivation from forge data, checked in this order: open question to the user, linked open pull request, assignee, otherwise open . If several labels of one tier match, the most urgent status wins ( blocked , needs_user , in_review , in_progress , open ), so the label order never matters. Derivation works on the data every adapter already reports (Forgejo/Gitea, GitHub, GitLab). Mapping Stored in settings.json as status_mapping : account id to an object {"<label>": "<status>"} . It is part of the settings backup ( docs/settings-backup.md ); files without the key load unchanged. Mappings of removed accounts are dropped on load, label names are trimmed and compared case-insensitively. Stale threshold Stored as stale : {"days": 3, "repos": {"<account id>": {"<owner/repo>": <days>}}} . An open issue without activity for days counts as stale; a repo entry overrides the global value. 0 or a missing key means the default (3 days), values are capped at 365, overrides of removed accounts are dropped. Settings page Settings, group "Work", row "Overview" ( settings-leitstand ) opens the page settings-leitstand-page : Stale: the global value ( settings-leitstand-stale-days-input ), then per account a list of the account's repos ( settings-leitstand-repos-<account> ); each repo has a days field (blank = same as all repos) and a reset button ( …-reset , disabled without an own value). Labels per account ( settings-leitstand-mapping-<account>-<status>-input ): your own labels per status, comma separated, with the recommended standard label shown below. A label entered for one status moves away from another, so it never stands for two. Fields save on blur or Enter through save_settings . Changes apply without a restart: when the mapping or the stale settings change, save_settings marks the cached overview data outdated, and the restarted account loops fetch it again on their next poll instead of after five minutes. For the UI RepoCounts.issues (dashboard rows) lists the open issues per repo with status.status and status.source ( mapping , standard_label , derived ).

Every counter in Gitoodo shows a value of one Counts value, computed in Rust ( crates/core/src/sync/counts.rs , SyncHub::counts in src-tauri/src/sync.rs ). The webview never counts on its own; it reads get_counts once and follows the counts event. Counter Value Tray title, Dock badge "needs you" (as the header) Tab "Fragen", header total + refused merges + status Heading "Fragen" questions , tasks , approvals Bundle "Freigabe" open approvals (#705) total = questions + tasks + approvals , so the single tab shows the tray number. Approvals of foreign contributions ( intake-approval-* cards) are no questions: the heading counts them apart, and the bundle above the list holds them. Tasks for the human are waiting items without a valid open question block ( needs-human with a description and maybe a - [ ] acceptance list, e.g. a step in a developer portal only a person can do; crates/core/src/human_task.rs ). They ask for a hands-on step, not a decision: the list shows them in their repo's group after its questions with the tag "Aufgabe" (#897), the sheet as "Aufgabe" with the checklist, "Erledigt" and "Zurück an den Orchestrator" (both with an optional note "Anmerkung (optional)"; on a hand-back the note is the person's instruction to the worker, see "Instructions" in docs/question-format.md ), and the heading names every kind that waits ("6 Fragen · 3 Aufgaben · 161 Freigaben"; only questions: "6 Fragen warten auf dich"). There is no inbox of forge notifications any more (#189): Gitoodo never fetches or marks forge notifications, and only waiting items are counted. The header shows no count (#84): each number appears once, on its tab. One "needs you" (#919). The header's overall state ("3 need you"), the badge on "Fragen an mich" and what that page lists on landing are one set, and a click on the header's number always lands on that page while the number is above zero: total (questions, tasks and approvals in scope, see "Autopilot scope" below), issues the autopilot gave up on ("Hängt fest", label stalled ) in repos with the autopilot on, except those the resolver still takes (its attempt queued, running or sure to come, decided in the core by resolver::takes ; docs/orchestrator/resolver.md , "In the app"): they wait behind the page's quiet "N the resolver is taking – show" ( resolverTakes ) and are in no count, listed on the page with their reason and "Try again", "Put back" and "View issue" (#919, see docs/states.md ). They are no approvals any more: a worker ran on them, so the issue never reads "waits for your approval" ( intake::reason ), ready issues in repos with the autopilot on that wait for a machine only the user can provide (an unknown host: , a machine with the wrong system, an expired agent sign-in), one each, listed on the page with their ways out ( repoNeeds(…).hosts , #919). The status part "workers" no longer counts these ( statusWaitCount ), so nothing counts twice, merges a repository setting refuses and the user still has to fix ( waitingBlocks , #942), the parts of the status only the user can fix ( countedParts : a rejected sign-in, a keychain approval, ready issues waiting for a worker machine, a service that does not answer, …), each shown as a card with its fixing action at the top of the page. A disk running low is left out (#970): it has its own entry in the status bar, its own notification and its problem on the status page. The repo part (questions in scope that are not answered yet, plus stalled issues and machine waits only the user can resolve in scope, repoNeedsCount ) comes from one place, repoNeeds over the sidebar's activity ( src/views/sidebar/repoActivity.ts ): the repos' marks ("3 issues need you") add up to it, and the header, the badge and the page use it, so the header always equals the sum of the repos' marks plus refused merges plus status problems, which have no repo mark. needsYouTotal in src/views/shell/overall.ts adds them up, and the header's tooltip names the parts ( needsYouHint , #1043: "In den Repos: 14 · Statusprobleme: 1"), so a number above the sum of the marks always says why (the button also carries it as its accessible description, since a tooltip alone never reaches screen readers); landing in src/views/questions/landing.ts is what the page lists, and needsYouCount.test.ts pins both to each other for a mix of questions, tasks, approvals, refused merges, machine notices, stalled issues, machine waits and repos with and without the autopilot. A way out taken on the page takes its issue out of every count at once ( markResolved in useRepoWorkspace.ts , for at most five minutes until the read model shows the change). Repos without the autopilot never feed the number : their questions, tasks and approvals wait behind the page's quiet "N more from repos without autopilot – show" at the end, and that N is never added anywhere. Tray and Dock show the same number. The window reports its "needs you" number to the app ( set_needs_you , from Shell.tsx ) whenever it changes; the tray title, its tooltip and, on macOS, the Dock badge (visible while the window has a Dock icon) show that number ( shown_total in src-tauri/src/tray.rs ). Before the window reported one, right after the start, they show the core's total . The main window is only hidden, never closed, so it keeps reporting while it is not on screen. Earlier the tray showed only total , so it could read 1 while header and badge read 22 (stalled issues and machine waits are no questions). Unseen items (the red tray check) still come from the core's Counts . Tray and webview are updated from the same Counts in the same call ( publish_counts ), after every poll, after answering or commenting, and after removing an account. Rule Questions : open entries of all "waiting for me" views, over all accounts, minus questions answered through the app (answer card or free comment) whose waiting_since is not newer than the posted comment. Such an answer is dropped at the next poll once the question has left the list or waits again. The popover shows the same questions teal ("handled"). These marks live in the core and count for every client (#1873): an answer from a paired phone sets the same mark as one from the window, so the counts drop at once, and every step (sending, answered, failed) reaches each window as the answered event, which the window's own marks follow ( get_answer_marks for a window that opens later). A failed post takes the mark back everywhere. One answer per item runs at a time; a second one that finds the mark is refused with already_answered and the place of the first answer instead of posting again (see docs/mobile.md , "Answered once"). Tray switch (#1376): every "waiting for me" view is polled and counts in the window (list, header, badges). A view's switch "Zähler in der Menüleiste/Taskleiste" ( counts_in_tray ) only decides whether its items also count in the tray and Dock: items found only by views with the switch off ( Counts::quiet , quiet_unseen ) are subtracted from the tray number and never turn the check red, and they get no notification or reminder. Kind ( account_counts , mirrored by waitKind in src/views/questions/tasks.ts ): an entry whose newest card is an intake approval is an approval; one without an open question block is a task; every other entry is a question. Each entry counts once. Overview (#237, #933), the start page: statistics only. It lists no questions and shows no "needs you" number; that number lives in the header and on "Fragen an mich". Repo rows with an open question (same rule) carry a mark without a number. No sidebar filter changes that number. Disabled repos (#135): items of repos switched off in the settings are in no list, no counter, no unseen mark and no system notification. They are dropped centrally ( without_disabled , read by SyncHub::tally and the snapshot events), so switching a repo off updates tray and lists at once; switching it on shows its items again (after the next sync for what the poll skipped). Ungated repos (#705): approvals of repos this app's orchestrator lists as observed or paused are in no counter and no list ( without_ungated , from Config::ungated ), since nothing works on them there; the paused intake asks no new ones. Repos it does not list keep their approvals. The other questions of those repos count as before. Autopilot scope (#897): in the orchestrator mode only repos with the autopilot on ( active in orchestration.json , Config::autopilot ) count. What waits in paused, observed or unlisted repos is in no counter, no unseen mark, no reminder, no chat notice and no system notification ( within_autopilot in SyncHub::tally and SyncHub::counted , within_scope for the toasts); the sidebar sets no "needs you" mark there either. The snapshot event names the repos ( autopilot ), so "Fragen an mich" lists those first, grouped by repo with the questions before the tasks, and keeps the rest behind "N weitere aus Repos ohne Autopilot – anzeigen" at the end. The direct mode and the setting asked_all_repos ("Fragen auch aus Repos ohne Autopilot", Settings → Notifications) count every repo ( autopilot is null ). Switching a repo's autopilot or the setting republishes counts and snapshots at once; an unreadable orchestration file hides nothing. List filters (search, repo, kind, status; #61) never change any counter. They narrow what a list shows, not what waits; otherwise the tray (which knows no filters) and the popover would disagree. Under an active filter only the head of the view says "shown of total" (e.g. "3 of 12 questions need you", #109); without a filter it shows the total. A failing account keeps its last good entries, so its counts stay stable until the next successful poll. Paging: every list request follows the forge's Link header ( collect_pages ), so counts are not capped at one page of 50. Seen and unseen Every counted item (open question) is either seen or unseen ( crates/core/src/store/viewed.rs , unseen_keys in counts.rs ). Seen means the item was visible in the opened list: its row stayed at least 60 % in view for about 0.7 s while the window was focused and visible. The webview only reports the keys ( mark_seen ); Rust looks up the item's activity time and stores it as the mark. New activity makes it unseen again : a question whose waiting_since is newer than its mark is unseen. Answered (handled) questions are never unseen. Snooze ( snooze_question , unsnooze_question ): a snoozed question leaves the list, the counters and the unseen marks until its wake-up time (presets: 1 hour, tomorrow 09:00 local, 1 week; computed in src/state/snooze.ts ). It returns by itself at that time (timer plus every poll), without restart. New activity on the issue does not wake it early. Stored per account in viewed.json ( snoozed , unix seconds); expired or vanished entries are pruned on the next poll. Tray : one unseen item turns the tray check red (macOS and Windows); the tooltip names how many, e.g. "Gitoodo (3, 1 unseen)". Counts.unseen carries the number. Lists : unseen rows carry a small neutral ink dot (6 px) and a hidden "Neu"/"New" for screen readers, never red. A dot stays while the user looks at the list and is gone once the window loses focus, so it never vanishes under the user's eyes. Persistence : marks live in viewed.json next to the settings and survive restarts. Marks of items that left the lists are dropped at the next poll; a removed account is forgotten. Local only : viewed.json is not part of the settings export and is never sent anywhere. System notifications A system notification appears only for a new hit of a "waiting for me" view that counts in the tray (assignment and labels as set in the criteria editor, #143). A plain new issue that no counting view matches never notifies, neither does a hit in a view that does not count, and an item in two counting views notifies exactly once (the hits are de-duplicated by repo and number in fetch_account ). Actions that wait for their data
b: The window is never empty after a start. It shows the last known state at once and replaces it part by part as the accounts and repositories answer. "Synced" only shows once every account has answered. Where the window opens The window opens on the start page: the statistics overview ( src/views/overview/OverviewView.tsx , docs/metrics.md , "Overview dashboard"), with what only the user can fix above the figures. The way back to it from anywhere is the first entry of the navigation, "Überblick" ("Overview", key 1), marked like every entry while the start page shows. The header shows the same full wordmark on every view, never a view title (each view names itself in its own heading), so the top of the window does not change when a repository or a page opens. The wordmark is a second way to the start page: a button named "Gitoodo, zum Überblick" ("Gitoodo, go to the overview"), reachable with Tab and pressed with Enter or Space. The introduction tour points at the navigation entry. What the next start opens ( src/state/lastView.ts , kept in the window's local storage, never in start-view.json ): Before the window closed Next start Nothing kept (first start, private mode, damaged entry) The start page. The start page, a tab ("All repos", "Asked of me", Chat) The start page. A repository's page, or a question or the settings opened on it That repository's page; Back leads to the start page. A repository that is gone since The start page. The onboarding handed over to the setup assistant The setup assistant over the start page. Why not the tab of earlier: the start page answers "is everything running?" in one look, which is the question at every start, and a list from earlier can have changed meanwhile. A repository is the exception: whoever closed the window inside one was in the middle of its work. "All repos" keeps its subpage, so the tab shows the page used last. A kept "Overview" subpage of earlier versions opens the start page. The view from earlier What is stored: a compact copy of what the window showed: the accounts (id, kind, label, address, login), each account's last good snapshot (questions and tasks, dashboard rows, repo list), the orchestrator's repositories (state and issues), the counts and the release planning's last report (#1694, the release plan and overview of the accounts still known). The releases keep the time they were read: a session that never opens the release view stores the ones from earlier again, with their old time, not as new. Errors are not stored; they belong to the moment. Where it lives: start-view.json in the app's state folder (the folder that also holds settings.json ). It is local only: it is not part of the settings export, and it is never sent anywhere. Who writes it: the window composes the view ( src/state/startView.ts ). The core stores it ( crates/core/src/store/start_view.rs ): fields whose names suggest a secret ( token , password , secret , cookie , credential , authorization , api_key , private_key , auth ) are dropped; every text passes the log redaction: registered tokens, token prefixes and URL credentials are replaced; the file stays under 4 MiB. A bigger view first loses issue bodies and comments, and a view that is still too big is not stored at all. When it is written: at most every 3 seconds while the window shows data that arrived since the start. The view from earlier alone is never stored again. Version: a view with another version, or a damaged one, is ignored whole, never shown in part. The next save replaces it. Figures of the start page (#1659) The start page's statistics come from reads of their own, not from the sync. So that the page does not start empty on every visit, it shows the figures of its last visit at once and lets a fresh read replace them in the background ( src/state/pageCache.ts , keys and checks in src/views/overview/cachedFigures.ts ): Figure Kept for Where Daily activity (tiles, today strip, bars, heat map) each scope: repos shown, days asked memory and the window's local storage Queue waiting time the week starts asked memory and the window's local storage App mode and dispatcher status (slots, usage) the running window memory only Per scope: an entry belongs to its repos and days, so figures of other filters or of yesterday never show; a new day reads anew. Activity is kept only from a read that is through (no repo still being read), so part of the repos never shows as too low figures. Up to six scopes per page are kept, the most recent ones. Only counts: the activity is kept without the read's progress (which names repos that failed), the queue waits only from a running dispatcher. The key names the repos in scope, as the kept last view does; no token, no forge text. Damaged or old: a store of another version, or an entry of a shape the page does not accept, is dropped without a message and read anew. Errors: a fresh read that fails shows its error as before; the kept figures are not kept on screen in its place. Drag repositories here…" Its count from earlier Questions The skeleton; once some arrived, shimmering rows under the list The questions from earlier; "As of 14:32" behind the heading Counters An empty shimmering pill, never "0" The counts from earlier Status bar "Loading repositories …", or "Loading 12 of 34 repositories …" once the totals are known Same Releases The loading line, or "busy" while the classifier's first poll runs The releases from earlier; "As of 14:32" in the place of the poll time (the hover explains it) Rules: "As of HH:MM": wherever data from earlier shows (sidebar, questions, releases), the label names when it was read, in local time; before today with the day, in another year with the year ( formatEarlier ). The sidebar and questions take the time the view was saved, the releases their own read time. The label goes as soon as fresh data replaces it: for the releases, the session's first report that shows something (an error keeps them in place, with the error). Synced: "Synced" (with its age) only shows once every account that the core polls has answered at least once since the start. A failed poll is also an answer; the error bar says why it failed. Until then the status bar counts the repositories that have answered. Unknown is not zero: a repository whose data has not arrived is a placeholder, never missing, "Empty" or a count of 0. "Only with work" keeps such repositories in the list until their data is known. A failed first poll keeps the data from earlier, still marked as from earlier. Repository by repository: the core reports each repository's progress as it is fetched (the repo-progress event: the account's listing first, then for each repository the start of each read and one event once it is through, with its dashboard row). The sidebar and the counts fill in as the events arrive, without waiting for the whole account. The core keeps the steps of each account's latest poll ( get_repo_progress ), and a window that opens while a poll runs replays them, so it knows the listings it did not hear. The start dialog While a start is not through, a dialog lies over every page ( src/views/shell/StartDialog.tsx , model in src/state/startDialog.ts , #1421). It lists the steps of this start, each with its state (waiting, running, done, error, or a note) and its progress, in words from the user's side: Signing in to accounts : "1/3" until every account is signed in: the forge accepted its token, which the listing of its repositories shows (or the account answered). The account's whole load is the next step. An account that answers with an error is retried by the sync; for 30 seconds the step only says "trying again", so a short network blip never shows as an error. Loading repositories : "12/33 (36 %)", or what loads right now while a repo list is still open ( src/state/loadPanel.ts ). It waits while no account is signed in. Starting background services : done once the app's own service step is through ( launch_state , src-tauri/src/launch_state.rs ) and every awaited service runs. When that step restarted the services (after an update), only what they wrote since counts; their activity from the old run never makes a start look finished. A service that is not up a minute later is an error. Looking through issues : the classifier's first full pass since it started: "12 of 33 repositories with autopilot" against the pass's own plan ( Request::Pass , PassProgress in crates/core/src/service_rpc.rs ): each account adds the repositories the pass reads once it listed them, so the total is fixed before the reads count up, and only finished reads count. After the last repository the pass still stores its picture; the step then says "Finishing …" without a count. A classifier that does not tell its plan shows only the running time. Reaching worker machines : "1/2" from DispatcherStatus.machines . A machine that does not answer 30 seconds after the dispatcher started is only a note: Gitoodo goes on without it. Handing out work : the first dispatcher round after the first look through the issues. A step that runs longer than 2 seconds shows its running time at the end of its line and a slim bar under it, so a fast start stays clean. The bar is filled when the source knows a count, with the count in words under the name ("12 of 31 repositories (38 %)"): signed-in accounts, loaded repositories, repositories the classifier read in this pass, reachable worker machines, and for handing out work the filled worker slots of those the queue can fill ( workers of min(max_workers, workers + queued) ). A running step never shows a full count: once its count is through, what is left has none, and the step says "Finishing …". Otherwise a faint band runs along the bar; with reduced motion a short block breathes in its middle instead, never a full bar. Under the intro one bar shows the whole start, with its percentage and, when known, the time left: "37 % · about 20 s left" ( src/state/startProgress.ts ). Each step weighs what it took at the last start (kept in the window's local storage: milliseconds per step, nothing else), else a typical share. A step adds its own share of done work only where it has a count; a step without one counts once it is done, so the percentage never pretends and never creeps towards 99 %. The bar never goes backwards: a step that turns out longer only slows it. The time left comes from this start's own rate where a count runs long enough to tell (2 seconds), from the last start's durations before that, and is left out when neither knows, e.g. at the very first start. The worker machines are reached beside the other steps, so their time does not add to the rest. Steps that do not apply are left out: without background services (store build, direct mode) only the first two; a service that is switched off or not set up is not awaited; with the orchestrator off, nothing the dispatcher does. The window is free once no step holds it. A step that failed or runs longer than usual (90 seconds, the look through the issues 3 minutes) offers "Go on without this step", an error also "View status" and "Open log". Tab stays inside. The dialog can always be closed, also while the first sign-in runs: with "Start now" at its foot, the close button at its top or Escape. Loading goes on; the window is usable at once. While the start still runs, the status bar shows a calm chip instead of its load line, "Still loading · 42 %" with a slim bar ( src/views/shell/StartChip.tsx , shared through src/state/startBackground.ts ); a click opens

Gitoodo writes a structured log to help explain what happened on a user's machine (for example a token check that failed, a worker that did not start, or a sync that keeps failing). The app and every background service (classifier, dispatcher with its worker supervision, satellite) use the same module ( crates/core/src/logging ) and schema. The log never contains tokens, Authorization headers, response bodies, or URL paths and queries; servers are logged as host[:port] only. Location One folder per user, shared by the app and the services: System Folder macOS ~/Library/Logs/de.gitoodo.app/ Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%\de.gitoodo.app\logs\ Linux $XDG_STATE_HOME/gitoodo/logs/ ( ~/.local/state/... ) GITOODO_LOG_DIR overrides the folder; with GITOODO_STATE_DIR set (tests, isolated runs) it is <state>/logs . The test-access build keeps its own folder under its identifier. File Writer gitoodo.log the app classifier.jsonl gitoodo classifier (also when the app starts it) dispatcher.jsonl gitoodo dispatcher , including the workers it supervises satellite.jsonl gitoodo satellite (not the --stdio bridge) <service>.stderr.log stderr of a service (bootstrap errors, a crash before logging started) runs/<run_id>/… terminal transcript of one worker run (see Worker transcripts ) Each process owns its file through a sidecar lock ( <file>.lock ). A second process of the same kind (for example a classifier service waiting for the app's classifier) writes <name>-<pid>.<ext> instead, so two processes never rotate one file. Each line is one JSON object (schema v 2): { "v": 2, "ts": "2026-11-16T11:00:11.175Z", "seq": 12, "level": "warn", "proc": "dispatcher", "pid": 4711, "component": "dispatch", "event": "dispatch.host_wait", "cid": null, "run_id": null, "issue": "owner/repo#42", "span": null, "audit": false, "msg": "waiting for a host; no matching host can take it", "ctx": { "host": "mac-mini", "reason": "offline" } } ts : UTC, RFC 3339 with milliseconds. seq : line number within the process, so gaps show dropped lines. proc : app , classifier , dispatcher or satellite ; pid the process ID. event : stable name; service events are dotted ( <area>.<what> ), app events keep their earlier names. msg is human text, never parsed. cid is a correlation ID: every line of one sync run (or one command) shares it. A cid field on an event (a classifier decision the dispatcher refers to) is lifted out of ctx . run_id , issue and span are top-level for every line ( null when unknown): a field of that name on an event is lifted out of ctx . run_id and span are reserved for timed worker runs (see Runs and steps ). ctx holds the remaining typed fields (at most 32), each redacted. Levels Level Meaning error Unrecoverable failure the user relies on (token check failed, keychain write failed) warn Failed, but retried or carried on (sync failed, integration error, keychain read failed) info State changes (sync finished, settings changed, audit events) debug Detail (sync started, every keychain access) Dependencies log only warn and error . Rotation, budget and retention Per file: 5 MiB, then the file becomes <file>.1 (older generations shift, beyond .3 they are deleted): at most 4 files and 20 MiB per process. A line that would not fit after a failed rotation is dropped rather than written past the cap (on Windows a file held open by a viewer cannot be renamed; Gitoodo then copies and empties it, and if that fails too it drops lines and retries after 30 s). The next written line reports the count as dropped_line . Whole folder: a disk budget, default 75 MiB (setting log_budget_mb , 20–500), covering every log and stderr file in the folder and one level of subfolders. Files older than 14 days (setting log_max_age_days , 1–90) are deleted. When the folder is over budget, the oldest files that no running process writes are deleted first. *.stderr.log files are emptied above 1 MiB. When: at the start of every process and every 6 h after ( log.cleanup names what was removed). Files of a running process are never deleted; their size is bounded by the per-file cap. gitoodo diagnose shows the folder's size against the budget. Service events Area Events every service service.started ( version ), service.stopped , service.fatal ( error ), panic ( location ), log.cleanup , service.binary_replaced ( component , installed , running ; Forge requests Every failed attempt of a forge request is one forge.request_failed line at warn: host (host[:port]), method , endpoint (the API route with every name, number and query replaced by * , for example /api/v1/repos/*/*/issues/*/comments ; never the path or the query), repo ( owner/name , when the route names one), status (HTTP, if any), kind (the token check categories below), attempt (1-based), outcome ( retrying , gave_up or not_retried ), retry_in_ms and repeats . Lines with the same host, method, endpoint and kind are throttled like other errors (see Throttling ). A request that succeeds after failed attempts logs forge.request_recovered ( attempts ). A 404 is an answer the callers handle (a deleted issue, an optional route), so it is logged at debug and counted in forge_not_found , not in forge_failures . The forge_* fields count, since the last summary: forge_requests sent, forge_cached reads answered without a request, forge_not_modified conditional reads the forge answered with 304, forge_failures failed attempts (rate limits included), forge_not_found 404 answers, and the retry wait and latency percentiles. A classifier poll reads each forge route once per account: inside the poll, repeated GETs (the reconcile pass, the queue snapshot and the read model read the same listings) are answered from memory, and a write to a repo makes the poll read that repo again. Replies with an ETag (GitHub, GitLab) are kept across polls and asked with If-None-Match . Forgejo and Gitea send no ETag ; there the comments of an issue whose updated_at and comment count did not change are reused for up to 10 minutes, and the complete issue listing of a repository is kept: a later poll reads only the forge's count of all issues and the issues updated since a minute before the last read ( since , by the forge's Date ), and reads the whole listing again when the count no longer fits (#1456). A dependency on a closed issue of that listing needs no lookup of its own. The cache lives in process memory only, keyed by a fingerprint of the credential, never by the token itself. Logs name the API family neutrally: gitea-compatible covers Forgejo and Gitea, which share the API and are not told apart without a signed-in request.
