h: The app language for macOS's own texts
b: Gitoodo shows every text in one language, chosen in Settings → General → Language. The window, the tray menu and tooltip, system notifications, user-facing errors and chat webhook messages always follow the same language and switch together at runtime, without a restart. Supported languages Tag Language Own name Direction Intl locale de German Deutsch left to right de-DE en English English left to right en-GB zh-Hans Chinese (Simplified) 中文（简体） left to right zh-Hans-CN hi Hindi हिन्दी left to right hi-IN es Spanish Español left to right es-ES ar Arabic العربية right to left ar German is the reference shape of the catalogue; English is the fallback. Choosing the language The setting is System or one of the tags above. It is stored in settings.json ( language ) and therefore part of the settings export and import (see settings-backup.md ). The frontend mirrors it in localStorage because the texts are needed before settings.json arrives. System walks navigator.languages and takes the first supported language. Regional variants map to their language: es-MX → es , zh-CN , zh-SG and zh-Hans → zh-Hans , ar-EG → ar , de-AT → de , hi-IN → hi . Traditional Chinese ( zh-Hant , zh-TW , zh-HK , zh-MO ) and every other language fall back to English. The picker shows each language in its own name, regardless of the current language. How texts are organised src/i18n/<namespace>.ts holds German and English for one area of the app ( shell , questions , dashboard , detail , settings , filter , permissions , native , support ). src/i18n/catalogue.ts lists the namespaces. src/i18n/locales/<tag>.ts holds one further language for all namespaces. Its type is Translation , so a missing or extra key is a compile error. t("namespace.key", vars) returns a text; {name} marks a variable. Numbers passed as variables are formatted in the digits of the language. tp("namespace.key", count, vars) returns a plural text. A plural is an object with one entry per CLDR plural category the language uses ( zero , one , two , few , many , other ); Intl.PluralRules picks the entry. Arabic uses all six, Chinese only other . Dates, times, relative ages and numbers go through Intl ( formatDate , formatDateTime , formatAge , formatNumber ). Never build them by hand. Texts shown by Rust The native namespace holds the texts of the tray menu and tooltip, system notifications and chat webhook messages. The frontend resolves them in the current language and sends them with the language's digits to the set_ui_texts command at start and on every language change ( src/App.tsx ). Rust rebuilds the tray menu right away and fills the placeholders itself. Until the first push, English applies. User-facing errors reach the frontend as categories and are translated there. Menu items macOS adds itself In window mode the menu bar follows the app language: Rust relabels Tauri's default menus and its own items (About, Settings…, Quit; src-tauri/src/app_menu.rs ). Some items are inserted by macOS itself and cannot be relabelled: Close All (File), Minimize All, Zoom All, Move & Resize, Full Screen Tile (Window), Writing Tools, AutoFill, Start Dictation… and Emoji & Symbols (Edit). AppKit localises them from the languages the bundle declares, CFBundleLocalizations in src-tauri/Info.plist (merged into the direct and the store build), so the list there must name every supported language (#1601). Empty .lproj folders are not needed. The app language for macOS's own texts The open and save panels (Cancel, New Folder, the sidebar and columns) and the menu items above are drawn by macOS from the languages the process starts with: AppleLanguages in the app's defaults, else the system's. The panel runs in a process of its own and takes that value only as it was at launch. So at every start, before AppKit or the webview read a language, src-tauri/src/process_language.rs writes the chosen language there, with the system region ( de-US for German on a US Mac, so week starts keep the region), and removes it again for System (#1121). A per-app language set in System Settings → General → Language & Region is replaced only for a chosen language; System removes only the value Gitoodo wrote itself (noted in GitoodoAppleLanguages ). A language change takes effect for these texts at the next start of the app; the window, tray and notifications switch at once. Because the webview then reports the chosen language in navigator.languages , the window resolves System from the shell's system_languages command (the system's list) instead. Right to left Arabic sets dir="rtl" and lang on the root element. To keep the layout correct in both directions: Use logical CSS properties ( margin-inline-start , padding-inline-end , inset-inline-start , text-align: start , border-inline-start ), never left / right . Horizontal motion multiplies by var(--dir-sign) ( 1 or -1 ). Icons that point along the reading direction ( back , chevron ) are listed in DIRECTIONAL in src/ui/Icon.tsx and mirrored by src/ui/Icon.css . Repository names, issue numbers, code and URLs stay left to right inside the text; wrap them in <bdi> or set dir="ltr" where they stand alone. Placeholders need nothing extra: in a right-to-left language t and tp wrap every text value in FSI/PDI, together with an @ or # written right before the placeholder ( @{login} , #{number} ), so "@alex", "~/gitoodo/repos" and "homelab/delta-web" keep their order. tFor (texts for the forge) stays plain. Paths and handles written into an Arabic text itself go between ⁦ and ⁩ (checked by i18n.test.ts ). Question format keywords The keywords of the question format ( Recommendation: , Deadline: , (yes/no) and the others in question-format.md ) are part of the machine-readable format and stay English in every language. Only their explanations in the UI are translated; answers are read in every supported language. Language on the forge What Gitoodo writes on the forge has its own setting (#980), Settings → Language → "Language on the forge" ( forge_language in settings.json ): app (default), issue or one of the six tags. A repository can override it in its repository settings → Questions ( forge_language of the repo in orchestration.json ). It covers the intake and approval questions and notes ( crates/core/src/orchestration/intake_texts.rs ), the dispatcher's closing notes on an empty pull request, its issue and gitoodo worker close ( crates/core/src/orchestration/close_texts.rs , #1889), the dispatcher's and classifier's other notes (superseded pull request, branch conflict, merged and waiting, an issue that waits for others, split and follow-up notes on the parent, dependencies closed, closed milestone, a stalled issue back in the queue; crates/core/src/orchestration/note_texts.rs , #1890), the answer hint of question headers, the fixed lines the app posts (finishing a task, the AI summary label, the suggested forward note; src/views/detail/forgeLang.ts ) and the worker brief, which names the language for question blocks, status notes and pull request texts. Code, commit messages and repository files follow the repository's own rules. app follows the app language. The services have no window, so System uses the language the window last resolved ( window_language in settings.json , written by the window, never by a settings save); before the first window, English. issue detects the language of the issue's title and body ( crates/core/src/forge_language.rs ). Code, links, mentions, issue references and identifiers are left out first. Arabic, Devanagari and Han script must make up at least 70 % of the letters (with a minimum length); Latin text needs at least eight words and enough common words of English, German or Spanish, clearly ahead of the other two. A short, mixed or other-language text falls back to the app language. The machine-read parts of the question format stay English in every case. Adding a language Add the tag to LANGS in src/i18n/define.ts (the order is the order of the picker). Add its Intl locale to LOCALES and its own name to ENDONYMS in src/i18n/index.ts . If the language is written right to left, extend direction . Map regional variants in matchLang if the base tag alone is not enough (as for Chinese). Create src/i18n/locales/<tag>.ts with export const <name>: Translation , translating every key. Give each plural the categories the language needs. Keep every {placeholder} and keep question-format keywords German. Register it in tables in src/i18n/index.ts and in the language union in src/core/types.ts . Add the variant to Language in crates/core/src/store/settings.rs (with a serde rename if the tag is not plain lowercase) and extend its test. Add the tag to SAME_AS_ENGLISH in src/i18n/i18n.test.ts with the keys that are intentionally identical to English (brand names, hosts). Run npm test : the guard checks key parity, plural categories, placeholders and untranslated values. Then check the layout in the real app at 400 px width for clipped labels. Translation style Natural and concise, as a native speaker would write a UI; no word-by-word translation. Labels must fit the 400 px window. Product name "Gitoodo" and forge names (GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, Forgejo) are never translated. Glossary One term per concept and language, so one screen never shows two names for the same thing (#1091). Every language keeps the loanword; Hindi writes it in Devanagari, Chinese in Latin letters with a space towards Chinese characters and without a plural. Concept de en es hi zh-Hans worker Worker worker worker वर्कर Worker repo Repo (Repository) repo (repository) repo (repositorio) रिपो (रिपॉज़िटरी) Repo issue Issue issue issue (el issue) इश्यू Issue The long form in brackets is the same word written out and may stand where German says "Repository". Not the term: es "trabajador", "incidencia"; hi Latin "worker", "repo", "issue" and "रेपो"; zh-Hans "工作进程", "工作者", "工作器", "仓库", "议题", and "问题" for an issue ("问题" is a question). Placeholders ( {repo} , #{issue} ), commands ( gitoodo worker pr ) and the settings search synonyms ( settingsNav.syn* ) are not prose and stay as they are. src/i18n/terminology.test.ts checks the catalogue against this list. Arabic says «طلب سحب» for a pull request (plural «طلبات سحب», dual «طلبا سحب» / «طلبَي سحب»), the term Arabic developer tools use; compact badges keep the Latin "PR", as English does. Not the term: «طلب دمج» (a GitLab merge request), transliterations and Latin words in running text (#1409).

Gitoodo can write its settings to a JSON file, read them back on another machine or after a reinstall, and undo the last import from an automatic backup. The UI lives in Settings → Backup ( src/views/settings/BackupPage.tsx ); the logic is in crates/core/src/store/transfer.rs and the Tauri commands in src-tauri/src/transfer.rs . File format { "app": "gitoodo", "schema_version": 2, "settings": { "...": "..." } } Field Meaning app Always gitoodo ; any other value is rejected as a foreign file. schema_version Settings schema the file was written with. settings The stored settings, accounts included, without any secret value. Older files are migrated in memory on import; the preview says so. Files from a newer schema are refused instead of being guessed at. The export is written atomically, so an interrupted export never leaves a half file behind. Suggested file name: gitoodo-settings-YYYY-MM-DD.json (local date). Secrets Tokens and the chat webhook URL live only in the keychain and never appear in an export, a backup, a preview or a log line. After an import, accounts whose token is missing in this machine's keychain show a "Replace token …" action ( accounts_needing_token ). The usage statistics choice and its random install ID live in usage.json , not in the settings, so they are never exported, imported or backed up: an imported settings file leaves the statistics undecided on the new machine, and a restored backup never brings back an install ID that was deleted by switching the statistics off ( docs/privacy.md , "Usage statistics"). Import in two phases Preview ( preview_settings_import ): the file is read, validated and migrated without changing anything. The preview lists the names of changed settings (never their values), added and removed accounts, accounts without a token and whether a migration ran. Apply ( import_settings ): after the user confirms, the current settings are written to the backup first, under the settings lock. If the backup fails, nothing is replaced. Then the imported settings are saved and theme, global shortcut and sync loops restart with them. Validation beyond the field types: every account needs a non-empty, unique id, a login and an http(s) address with a host. Automatic backup and restore Every import writes the previous settings to settings.backup.json next to the settings file. settings_backup_time returns the backup's time (Unix ms) or nothing; the UI shows it or a "no backup" hint. restore_settings_backup backs up the current settings before restoring, so a restore can itself be undone. Limits and errors Reason When too_large File over 1 MiB; it is refused without reading. not_json Not valid JSON. foreign_file app is not gitoodo . newer_version Schema newer than this build supports. invalid_content Validation failed; detail capped at 200 chars. no_backup Restore without a backup. io File access or encoding failed. The frontend maps these to its own rejection keys ( rejection() in src/views/settings/transfer.ts ) and shows a calm, localised message. Import, export and restore are recorded as audit events without content. Test IDs settings-backup-export , -import , -preview , -preview-migrated , -confirm , -confirm-yes , -cancel , -status , -renew , -restore , -restore-none , -restore-time , -restore-open (all prefixed settings-backup ).

One rule for every file and folder the app reads or writes (settings, state files, backup, logs, export and import files): Follow links for reading and writing, absolute or relative, for single files and for whole folders (config/data folder, log folder). Never replace a link with a file. Atomic saves write the temp file next to the link's target and rename it over the target; the link stays. Corrupt-file recovery leaves the link in place and copies the target's content to <name>.corrupt next to the link. Never delete a link target. Log rotation of a linked gitoodo.log copies the content to .1 and empties the target; deleting rotated files removes only the link itself. Refuse where following is unsafe. A dangling link or a link loop is reported as an error ("points to ... which does not exist; nothing was written" / "loops back on itself"); nothing is created at the link's target. Logging swallows the error and retries later. Implementation: crates/core/src/links.rs ( resolve_link ), used by store/fsutil.rs and logging/writer.rs . Export and import go through the same helpers, so the path returned by the file picker may be or contain a link. Platforms Linux/macOS direct build: covered by unit tests (linked file, linked folder, relative, dangling, loop). macOS sandboxed store build: a link outside the container only works if the user granted access to its target; the scoped-folder bookmark must be created for the resolved folder. Not verified on a device (documented only). Windows: symlinks and junctions are followed by the OS for folders; file links are resolved by resolve_link . Creating them needs developer mode or admin rights, so the tests are Unix-only. Not verified on a device (documented only).

How the popover window is framed per platform and build type, and why the App Store build stays free of private API. Code: src-tauri/src/frame.rs and frame_macos.rs (native side), src/ui/tokens.css (block "Window frame"). Per platform Build Frame Corners macOS direct transparent window over Liquid Glass (macOS 26+) or the popover material rounded, 12 pt macOS App Store solid, the page paints --color-bg , normal window shadow rounded, 12 pt Windows 11 solid rounded by DWM Windows 10, Linux solid square Plain browser solid (no data-frame from the shell) n/a The shell sets data-frame="vibrancy" or data-frame="solid" on <html> through an initialization script, so the first paint already matches. Only vibrancy lets the material show through; every other value keeps the solid tokens. Store build: no private API A transparent webview needs WebKit's private key drawsBackground (wry sets it whenever Tauri asks for transparent ). App Store review rejects private API, so the store build keeps an opaque webview and only rounds the window ( Frame::Rounded ): The main window is declared with "create": false in tauri.conf.json and built in frame::create_main . Transparency and effects are only requested when frame_for(Platform::Mac, store = false) returns Vibrancy . The store build (Cargo feature store ) never calls transparent , so the private key is never touched and the frame is the normal opaque window. macOSPrivateApi stays off in every config. Corners: frame_macos::round_corners gives the window's content view a layer ( NSView.wantsLayer ) with CALayer.cornerRadius = frame::CORNER_RADIUS , cornerCurve continuous and masksToBounds , so the webview is clipped. The window turns non-opaque with a clear background ( NSWindow.isOpaque , NSWindow.backgroundColor = NSColor.clearColor ): only the clipped corners are see-through, the page still paints --color-bg behind every pixel, so the frame stays solid (also with Reduce transparency). Shadow: kept on ( NSWindow.hasShadow , then invalidateShadow ). For a non-opaque window macOS derives the shadow from the drawn pixels, so it follows the rounded corners; the square outline of the direct build does not occur here because there is no effect view in the square frame. No unsafe : the NSWindow is looked up among NSApplication.windows by comparing it with Tauri's ns_window() handle, so no raw pointer is dereferenced. All calls are safe objc2 bindings ( objc2-app-kit , objc2-quartz-core ); kCALayerCornerCurveContinuous is passed by its documented string value continuous instead of reading the extern static. No window-vibrancy setCornerRadius and no NSVisualEffectView / NSGlassEffectView in this build; translucency there is a separate spike. The string drawsBackground still exists in the binary as a constant in wry's code; that branch only runs for transparent , which the store build never requests. It is no Objective-C selector ( __objc_methname does not contain it). Public API used (Apple documentation): NSView.wantsLayer , NSView.layer , CALayer.cornerRadius , CALayer.cornerCurve , CALayer.masksToBounds , NSWindow.isOpaque , NSWindow.backgroundColor , NSColor.clearColor , NSWindow.hasShadow , NSWindow.invalidateShadow() , NSApplication.windows . macOS direct build Effects list [LiquidGlassRegular, Popover] , state Active , radius frame::CORNER_RADIUS (12 pt, mirrored as --radius-window ). Tauri applies the first effect the system supports: macOS 26 and later: NSGlassEffectView with its public cornerRadius . macOS 15 and older: NSVisualEffectView with the popover material; the corner radius goes through window-vibrancy's undocumented setCornerRadius . Acceptable only because this build is not reviewed by Apple; it is the second reason the store build stays solid. No window shadow ( shadow(false) ). macOS computes the shadow from the square window frame, not from the rounded material, which left a square dark outline around the corners. The page paints a veil over the material ( --color-window , 55 % of the solid ground) so text keeps the solid contrast values in light and dark. Dark mode adds a 1 px light inner edge so the window separates from dark wallpapers without a shadow. The veil sits on #root with border-radius: var(--radius-window) , never on body : with a transparent <html> , a body background propagates to the whole square canvas and fills the corners. Reduce transparency ( prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce ): macOS draws the material opaque and the veil switches to --color-bg , so the window is solid with the regular contrast. Windows and Linux Opaque windows with the page background. Windows 11 rounds undecorated windows itself (DWM, shadow: true from the config). Windows 10 and Linux stay square; no effect API is used there. Since the frame is solid , the page never draws an inner card here: the popover is the DWM-rounded window itself, and the detached window is a normal decorated window with the page edge to edge (checked on Windows 11, light and dark, #248). Window and tray Gitoodo is a regular app window with a tray icon beside it; docking the window to the icon is a choice (#1614). Code: src-tauri/src/window_mode.rs , login_start.rs , settings docked and autostart_hidden (core store/settings.rs ). Default: a regular, decorated window with a Dock icon (macOS) or taskbar entry, shown at start in its stored frame (see "Detached window"). The tray icon always exists; its click and its menu (open, sync, pause or resume the autopilot, settings, services, quit) work in every mode. Closing the window (close button, Alt+F4) never quits: the window hides and Gitoodo keeps running in the tray. On macOS the app then drops its Dock icon (accessory app) and gets it back when the window opens again. Quit is in the tray menu. Docked (Settings, General, "Dock to the menu bar" / "Dock to the taskbar", off by default): the window is the tray-anchored panel that hides on blur, as before; the header button shell-detach and Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+D turn it into the window and back (see "Detached window"), closing the detached window docks it again. Without docking the header has no such button and the shortcut does nothing. Switching docking off turns an open panel into the window at once; switching it on docks the window the next time it closes (or at once when it is not shown). Start state: a start by hand always opens the window (docked: the app starts at its icon, as before). A start at sign-in stays in the tray only when the user chose "At login, start in the menu bar only" ( autostart_hidden , shown below "Start at login" while not docked). Detection ( login_start::detect , read once early in the start-up): the autostart plugin's entries (Windows setup install, Linux, macOS outside an app bundle) pass --autostart ; older entries without it are rewritten on the next start ( autostart::system::refresh ). The macOS login item ( SMAppService , both direct and App Store build) passes no arguments; its launch is the "open application" Apple event with keyAEPropData = keyAELaunchedAsLogInItem , read via NSAppleEventManager.currentAppleEvent . The MSIX startup task passes neither, so there the window always opens. Second start: the single-instance plugin (and on macOS the App Store build, without that plugin, the system's reopen event) brings the running window to the front. Migration: installations from before this choice have neither field and get the regular window; the panel was the only mode before, not a choice anyone made. UI automation opens the docked panel at start without a tray click and keeps the Dock icon; the hidden start at login applies as in the normal build (start with --autostart to check it). Resizing The docked popover keeps its tray-anchored, title-bar-free look and can still be resized by dragging any edge or corner. Code: src-tauri/src/window_size.rs , tray::place_main , core store/window.rs . Native resizing, no extra grip: the window is "resizable": true with "decorations": false . macOS: tao uses the style mask Borderless | Resizable , so AppKit offers the invisible resize edges and corners of a normal window, in both builds. Windows: tao hit-tests the undecorated window ( WM_NCHITTEST ) and, with the DWM shadow on, keeps the invisible resize borders outside the page, so every edge and corner works. Bounds: at least 400 x 320 logical points ( minWidth / minHeight in tauri.conf.json ); at most the work area of the screen the tray icon is on ( set_max_size each time the window opens). store::fit_size applies both bounds to the remembered size; on a screen smaller than the minimum the minimum wins and the placement keeps the top-left corner on screen. Size: the popover always opens in the remembered size (default 400 x 680 until the user resizes it); the page never reports a content height and nothing resizes the window on its own. Placement: tray::place_main gives the window its fitted size first and then centres it below (menu bar) or above (bottom taskbar) the tray icon with that size, clamped to the work area, so it never leaves the screen. Without an icon rect the positioner plugin places it as before. Persistence: window.json in the app config directory (logical points, versioned like the other stores, corrupt or missing file gives the default). The size is stored when the window hides and when the app quits, only if the user changed it: a size the app shrank to fit a smaller screen does not overwrite the wish for a larger one. Local to the installation: settings export and import do not carry it. Reset: Settings, General, "Window size", button settings-window-size-reset (command reset_window_size ) stores the default and resizes an open window in place at the tray icon. Frame at any size: the vibrancy material (direct build) and the content view's rounded layer (store build) resize with their views; the store build recomputes its pixel-derived shadow after every resize ( frame::resized , NSWindow.invalidateShadow() ). The page has no fixed widths; lists, detail and settings fill the extra space, centred empty states keep a readable measure. Detached window The regular window (the default, see "Window and tray") and the docked popover turned into a window share this frame and behaviour. Code: src-tauri/src/window_mode.rs , core store/detached.rs . Detach: header button shell-detach or Cmd+Shift+D (macOS) / Ctrl+Shift+D (Windows, Linux), command detach_window . The same window changes its style, so the page keeps its state: title bar, task bar entry (Dock icon on macOS), not always on top, freely resizable (at least 400 x 320, no upper bound) and no longer hidden on blur. The tray icon and its click keep working and bring the window to the front. Back (docked only): header button shell-attach , the same shortcut, or closing the window (red button, Alt+F4). The window hides and turns back into the popover; the app keeps running in the tray. Without docking, closing only hides the window. Quit stays in the tray menu. Frame: position and size are stored in detached-window.json whenever the window goes back (and before quit), in logical points of the desktop. store::place_detached reopens it there when enough of it lies on a current screen (shrunk to that screen), otherwise at 900 x 700 centred on the main screen (shrunk to its work area on a smaller screen). Local to the installation like window.json . End of the onboarding (#617): its fixed, centred window (never stored as the frame) becomes the detached window in the stored frame, else the default, and stays in front ( finish_onboarding_window ); the overview and the pending introduction tour open in it, or the setup assistant after an orchestrator run. Closing it returns to the tray like any detached window. It does not switch back to the tray panel: on macOS that made the app an accessory app, which resigned it active, and the blur dismissed the freshly shown panel at once, so nothing appeared. Size: a size the user dragged is the stored frame; the popover keeps its own s

h: Prompt timing and behaviour when denied
Notifications on macOS: prompt shown in the background (#166)
Folder access and background items on macOS (#1250)
Background services read the token without a prompt (#369)
b: Which permissions Gitoodo needs on macOS and Windows, per build type, when the system asks, what the app does when the user declines, and where the decision comes from. Principle (Apple HIG "Privacy", Microsoft "Windows app privacy guidance"): ask in context, only when the feature needs it, explain calmly before the system prompt, and never block the app when a permission is denied; show a hint that leads to the system settings. Build types: macOS direct: Developer ID, hardened runtime, notarized, not sandboxed ( Entitlements.direct.plist ). macOS App Store: sandboxed ( Entitlements.appstore.plist , Cargo feature store , config overlay tauri.appstore.conf.json ). Windows direct: unpackaged installer, full trust. Windows MSIX: packaged for the Microsoft Store ( src-tauri/windows/AppxManifest.template.xml ). Matrix Purpose macOS direct macOS App Store Windows direct Windows MSIX Network to forges (HTTPS) no entitlement needed com.apple.security.network.client none capability internetClient Forge on the local network Local Network prompt ( NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription ); ATS NSAllowsLocalNetworking same, plus network.client none (firewall prompt is the system) privateNetworkClientServer Skill install into agent skills folders writes directly (not sandboxed) folder dialog ( files.user-selected.read-write ), explanation first writes directly writes directly ( runFullTrust ) Desktop control (Agent Desktop) Accessibility and Screen Recording for Gitoodo Service, requested by the app; see Agent Desktop not available (no npm, no SSH in the sandbox) a signed-in, unlocked session not available in the Store build Screenshot from the app (#1857) Screen Recording for Gitoodo, asked by macOS on the first "Screenshot"; without it the picture shows only the desktop and Gitoodo's own windows same; /usr/sbin/screencapture runs inside the sandbox (not yet tried in a sandboxed run) not offered (paste with Win+Shift+S, Ctrl+V) not offered Notifications UNUserNotificationCenter , authorization at start or first send; denial shown same (sandbox needs no entitlement) no prompt; hint to Notifications settings same Start at sign-in SMAppService.mainApp in the app bundle (macOS 13+, #1250); hint to Login Items. See Folder access and background items SMAppService.mainApp (macOS 13+) autostart plugin (registry) windows.startupTask , see store Menu bar / tray only, no Dock icon LSUIElement LSUIElement none none Tokens Data protection keychain (group entitlement + profile), file-based fallback; see Keychain same group; see Keychain Credential Manager, no prompt Credential Manager, no prompt Prompt timing and behaviour when denied Local network (macOS): the system asks on the first connection to a local host and holds the connection while its prompt is open; the prompt can sit behind the app window. The app does not pre-prompt. When a forge check (account wizard in settings, onboarding and worker accounts, and the token replacement dialog) of a local forge runs longer than 3 s, a calm note names the prompt and the way to System Settings › Privacy & Security › Local Network (#1207). When the connection fails as unreachable, the error reads "cannot reach the server on your local network" instead of "server unreachable", with a note on how to allow the access later or check the server; both notes carry "Systemeinstellungen öffnen" ( Privacy_LocalNetwork ). Only for local hosts on macOS ( local_network_hint_applies : .local , .lan , .home.arpa , .internal , single-label names, private and link-local IPv4/IPv6, also typed without scheme); loopback never asks, so it gets no note. Notifications (macOS): Gitoodo asks for alert and sound authorization at start once an account and a notification type are set up, and again before every send (the system only prompts while undecided). The settings page reads the state the same way: on a denial it says so ("Mitteilungen sind ausgeschaltet"), otherwise it keeps the general note; both lead to the Notifications pane. See Notifications on macOS . Notifications (Windows, Linux): the Tauri notification plugin reports the permission as granted, so a denial cannot be detected; the page keeps the general note with the action "Systemeinstellungen öffnen" ( ms-settings:notifications ). A failed send is logged. Start at sign-in: toggled by the user on the autostart page. When it fails (denied or pending approval in Login Items), the page shows the error with the action "Systemeinstellungen öffnen" ( com.apple.LoginItems-Settings.extension , ms-settings:startupapps ). First-run onboarding (#94, #617): shown on first launch, whenever no account exists, and from "Hilfe & Feedback → Erste Schritte". It runs in its own centred window (980 x 680, clamped to the screen; its frame is never stored as the window frame) with named phases on top: Willkommen, Konto, Repos, Arbeitsweise, Mitteilungen & Start, Fertig. Enter runs the main action and Esc goes back, except in text fields. The repo step switches repos on or off with the same disabled_repos as Settings → Repos and leaves orchestration rules alone. Its notification step asks only on the button "Mitteilungen erlauben" and shows the denied hint with the Notifications pane; its autostart step (on by default) shows the same error and Login Items action as the autostart page. Progress is stored in the settings ( onboarding ), so every step can be skipped and an interrupted run resumes; closing the window pauses it and the next tray click reopens it. Finishing ("Zum Überblick", or "Orchestrator einrichten" for the setup assistant) turns the window into the regular detached window ( finish_onboarding_window , see docs/window-frame.md ), where the overview and the introduction tour (or the setup assistant) follow. Skill folder (App Store build only): the skill page explains why ~/.claude is needed and what is written (only gitoodo-questions ), then opens the folder dialog. A folder not named .claude is rejected with a hint; cancelling changes nothing. The direct build skips this step. The system settings deep links are in src-tauri/src/permissions.rs ( settings_url ). Notifications on macOS (#131) Symptom: on macOS 27 no notification appeared and Gitoodo was missing from System Settings > Notifications. Root cause: the Tauri notification plugin (2.x) posts through notify-rust and mac-notification-sys , which use the deprecated NSUserNotificationCenter . Before the first post, mac-notification-sys looks up a bundle id with an AppleScript ( get id of application ... , blocked in the sandbox and failing anyway), falls back to com.apple.Finder / com.apple.Terminal and swaps the implementation of NSBundle.bundleIdentifier . Notifications were therefore posted under another app's identity; Gitoodo never registered with Notification Center and never asked for authorization. The plugin spawns the post and returns success, and its desktop permission check always answers "granted", so nothing was logged. Fix: on macOS the plugin is not linked any more. src-tauri/src/notify_macos.rs uses UNUserNotificationCenter through the safe objc2-user-notifications bindings (no unsafe ): requestAuthorizationWithOptions (alert, sound), then addNotificationRequest with a unique identifier. It only runs inside an .app bundle (an unbundled cargo /dev binary would make the center raise); outside, a warning is logged and nothing is posted. Failures are logged as notification_error with a reason ( authorization_failed , rejected , no_app_bundle ), never with the notification text. Windows and Linux keep the plugin and now log a failed send. Limits: the error object of a failed request is not read (that would need unsafe ), so the log has the reason but not the system's error code. Only a click asks (#1215): the "Allow notifications" buttons of the onboarding and of Settings → Notifications request authorization and take the state from its answer. Nothing else asks: the app start no longer requests authorization (#166 did, for configured installs), and a post reads the decision from UNNotificationSettings without asking and is skipped while it is undecided ( notification_skipped , reason undecided ) or denied. The notifications page reads the same state ( notification_status , undecided shows the button instead of the system settings hint); opening it used to request authorization and so showed the system prompt without a click. The read needs unsafe and lives in crates/scoped-folder ( authorization ). There is no notification-center delegate, so a banner may be held back while Gitoodo's own window is in front. Notifications on macOS: prompt shown in the background (#166) Symptom: after #131 the permission request did not appear and Gitoodo was missing from System Settings > Notifications. Evidence (unified log of the installed, Developer ID signed, sandboxed /Applications/Gitoodo.app , macOS 27.2): usernoted registers the bundle at the first request ("Sending request for permission for <bundle id>"), but the prompt record is alertStyle:"none" with response action: closed and the settings read authorizationStatus: Denied ; the authorization was only set to "allow" seven seconds later, by hand. Signing, bundle identity and sandbox are therefore fine: the center is reached ( Creating a user notification center , didGrant ) and later banners were delivered ( Presenting ... alertStyle:"banner" ). The app log has no notification_* event because nothing failed. Cause: the request is made at start from a menu-bar app ( LSUIElement , accessory policy) that is not the active app, so the system shows the prompt as a quiet banner that closes by itself. It is counted as not allowed, and the user never saw a dialog. Fix then: the first authorization request at start activated the app first. Superseded by #1215: the app no longer asks at start at all; the request comes from a click on "Allow notifications", when Gitoodo's window is the active one, so the prompt is shown as a dialog. A leftover notification-prompted marker file in the config dir is no longer read. Open: without a notification-center delegate a banner is still held back while Gitoodo's own window is in front (needs unsafe , which the crate forbids). Folder access and background items on macOS (#1250) macOS guards some folders of the home folder with a privacy prompt ("Gitoodo would like to access files in your Desktop folder"): Desktop, Documents and Downloads, iCloud Drive, other apps' data and removable and network volumes. Listing such a folder is enough to ask, the answer belongs to the app identifier (an update keeps it; the change from online.lindstedt.gitoodo to de.gitoodo.app does not), and an unexplained prompt is a defect. Gitoodo opens a guarded folder only where the user put something of Gitoodo's: a folder named under "Do you already have checkouts?" ( dispatch.projects_folders ), the clone folder, a working copy set for a repo, or the worktree folder. The app and the background services read those, and macOS asks once per identifier for each guarded folder among them (picking a folder in the folder dialog covers only the app process; a service asks on its own first access). That prompt follows the user's own choice. The defaults ( ~/gitoodo/repos , ~/gitoodo/worktrees ) are not guarded. The suggestions of the onboarding's copies step come from a short scan of the home folder ( checkouts::scan_home ). On macOS it never opens Desktop, Documents and Downloads, as it never opens Library (iCloud Drive and other apps' data live there), media and cloud-sync folders. Before this rule the scan caused the Desktop and Documents prompts on a first setup. The step never ends in silence (#1114): it says when the scan found nothing or failed, names the folders it left out with why, and offers "Search these folders too". Only that button opens them ( checkouts::scan_guarded ), so macOS asks right after the user's own click; a folder macOS refuses is named with the way out (System Settings › Privacy & Security › Files a

t: Test access: driving the app without a human
h: A real test repository beside the fixture
Check that every element has a test ID
Restore the desktop after a test
b: The normal app drops its Dock icon while its window is closed to the tray (then it is hidden from the accessibility tree) and, docked to the tray icon, opens only on a tray click and hides on blur. The test access build removes those obstacles so a worker can operate it with Agent Desktop ( agent-desktop , see below). It is a separate Cargo feature ( test-access ); release and store builds contain none of it. What the test build changes: Window mode : a regular, decorated window, visible at start, never dismissed on blur. The app is a Dock app, so agent-desktop list-windows lists it as Gitoodo Test . It opens in the detached window's frame (remembered, else 900 x 700 centred, clamped to the screen; #363), not in the popover size ( docs/window-frame.md , "Test build"). Own identity : bundle ID de.gitoodo.app.testaccess , own config and log directory. It runs next to the installed app and never touches it (single instance, keychain, settings). Several test instances run side by side with their own folders (see "Folders and parallel instances"). Test account : a fixture forge ( fixture/demo , user tester ) and an in-memory token store. No real token, no network, no keychain. The account keeps the fixed id acc-fixture across restarts, so per-account state such as folded groups persists; other accounts are removed. Own keychain service : the secrets the test build does keep in the keychain (chat webhook, remote machine passwords) live under the service gitoodo.testaccess , never under the production service gitoodo ( src-tauri/src/keychain.rs , #1192). Saving, testing or clearing them leaves the entries of an installed Gitoodo unchanged. Test IDs in the accessibility tree : each data-testid is mirrored into the DOM id (Agent Desktop's native_id of kind ax_dom_identifier , searchable with find --native-id ) and into aria-roledescription . An element that already has its own id (label association) keeps it. A screen reader speaks that role description in place of the role ("shell-settings" instead of "button"); for a screen-reader check start the test app with GITOODO_TEST_REAL_ROLES=1 , which keeps the page's own roles and leaves out the mirror (#1163). Address controls by name then. Notifications : the permission reads as granted; posts are logged as test_notification . Usage statistics : hard stop. The test build, like any run with GITOODO_UI_AUTOMATION=1 , records, writes and sends nothing, whatever the onboarding switch says ( docs/privacy.md ). Build and start VITE_TEST_ACCESS=1 npx tauri build --debug --bundles app \ --features test-access --config src-tauri/tauri.test-access.conf.json open -n "target/debug/bundle/macos/Gitoodo Test.app" The panel is open right away. Nothing needs a tray click. Address elements by test ID Scripts use Agent Desktop. Point GITOODO_AGENT_DESKTOP at it (default: agent-desktop on PATH, which Gitoodo installs as ~/.local/bin/agent-desktop ); the scripts in this repo never hardcode its location. Workers go through gitoodo desktop [--on NAME] <command> instead, which waits for their turn at that machine's desktop and reaches another machine's desktop over SSH ( dispatcher ). agent-desktop find --app "Gitoodo Test" --native-id shell-settings --first # exact test ID agent-desktop click @<snapshot>:e<n> # ref from the line above Every command prints one JSON envelope; matches carry ref_id ( @<snapshot>:e<n> ), role , name and native_id . Refs belong to one snapshot; the test ID does not change. snapshot --app "Gitoodo Test" prints the whole tree ( --max-depth 50 for deep screens). Ref actions are headless: they neither move the pointer nor take the focus. Look again after each action. One session at a time uses a desktop. Workers take turns through gitoodo desktop-turn ; a script is run while nobody else uses this desktop. Fixture content: three questions in fixture/demo . #1 has a question block with a deadline (tomorrow), #2 is free text, #3 has a deadline two days in the past (the overdue label of the list, #73). GITOODO_TEST_EXTRA_QUESTIONS=<n> at start adds n free-form questions (#4 on, at most 200) to check many open questions (#237). Rows are questions-row-… , copy and share buttons are questions-copy-… and questions-share-… , the detail screen uses detail-… . For long-string layout checks (#337), set GITOODO_TEST_LONG_TEXT=1 . Every fixture title (default, scale and showcase mode; in the showcase also the board, session and release titles of the orchestrator's read model, #1161) gains a long sentence and one long word without break opportunities, so wrapping, clipping and ellipses show at the minimum window size. Bodies, numbers and labels stay unchanged. For large-list navigation (#337), set both GITOODO_TEST_REPOS=300 and GITOODO_TEST_ISSUES_PER_REPO=5 in the test app's launch environment. This replaces the default fixture with 300 repositories ( fixture/scale-001 through fixture/scale-300 ) and 1,500 distinct issues. Each issue is assigned to tester , has needs-human and a cycling ready , in-progress , in-review or blocked status label. Question bodies reuse the three default question types. Each repo also has two fixture pulls, with the green pull linked to that repo's first issue. Dashboard groups and counts come through the normal Rust adapter and sync path. Both values must be positive integers; missing, invalid or zero input keeps the default fixture and its existing extra-question behavior. Valid scale inputs are capped at 300 repos and 20 issues per repo (6,000 issues total); GITOODO_TEST_EXTRA_QUESTIONS is ignored in scale mode. The scale dataset is seeded once at startup. Repo names, forge IDs and issue URLs are unique; issue numbers are globally unique within this fixture. Comments and closures are scoped to their repository and remain in memory until exit. Other unsupported adapter mutations stay unsupported. This creates test data, not a performance result; navigation and responsiveness still need an explicit runtime check. For clarity checks with many repositories (#1165), add GITOODO_TEST_SIMILAR_NAMES=1 to a scale launch. Repo i becomes <owner>/<stem>-<nnn> : the owner cycles through fixture , fixture-platform-engineering and fixture-archive , the stem through four long names that share their start ( customer-portal-backend-service , …-integration-tests , customer-portal-frontend , …-legacy ). Every short name exists under all three owners and names differ only at their end, so a cut name or a missing owner shows. Issues keep their numbers and follow their repo. GITOODO_TEST_VARIED=1 (repo n keeps per_repo - n issues, at least one, and only its first waits for a human) combines with it. Showcase data for screenshots GITOODO_TEST_FIXTURE_LANG=de or =en replaces the fixture with an invented open-source team in that language ( src-tauri/src/test_showcase.rs ): three repositories ( kiezwerk/pegelstand , kiezwerk/radkeller and kiezwerk/hofladen , in English harborlight/tidewatch , harborlight/trailkit and harborlight/driftlog ), four questions to the user (one with a deadline tomorrow, one free text, one overdue, one approval), the board with three running workers, pull requests (one with a failing ci/test ), a week of closed issues and merged pulls for the weekly review, eight weeks of throughput, the readiness checklist of a well kept repo and a scripted orchestrator chat that proposes one comment. Workers, usage, setup checks and the chat are answered by the fixture, never by a running classifier, dispatcher or agent. A simulated dispatcher ( src-tauri/src/test_showcase_dispatcher.rs , #915) gives each session a live terminal over the real attach protocol (backlog, a step line every few seconds, typed keys echo back) and applies steering: Hold and Resume mark the worker held, an instruction appears in its terminal, Cancel, Stop and Park end it, Restart counts a restart. Any other value keeps the plain fixture above. The first two repositories plan two releases each (#1552, #1540), all with due dates. The first one: 1.4 , the next one, with open, running and three merged issues plus the sub-issues #221 and #226 , which their parent #224 depends on and pulls in (#1530), and 1.5 with one. The second one: 2.0 , the next one, with a running, an open and two merged issues, and 2.1 with one. The third repository plans no release; the extra sessions' issues are in none either. Each planning repository holds the tag of an earlier release ( 1.3 , 1.9 ): naming a release like it in "Bearbeiten …" shows the warning about an existing tag. The fixture forge keeps the milestones in memory, so the release dialogs work on them until the app exits: issues are added, moved and taken out, releases are created, edited, closed and removed (no forge releases exist), and the release view, the board's release chips and the autopilot's release focus follow at once. GITOODO_TEST_SHOWCASE_SESSIONS=N (with the showcase) runs N sessions in total instead of three, at most 24: the extra ones are in-progress issues numbered from 300 in both repositories, for checks of a crowded session grid. GITOODO_TEST_SHOWCASE_BACKLOG=N (with the showcase) adds N ready issues in no release to the first repository, at most 300, numbered from 1000: a long list in "Issues hinzufügen" for checks of the release dialogs, e.g. adding more issues than one membership change takes (100, #1685). Three switches drive the failure and slow paths of the showcase for real-app checks (#1218): GITOODO_TEST_CHAT_PAUSE_MS=<ms> pauses that long between the events of a scripted chat turn (default 250, at most 60000), so a long turn can be watched; GITOODO_TEST_CHAT_SEND_FAIL=1 makes the first chat message fail to reach the session; GITOODO_TEST_WRITE_FAIL=1 makes the first fixture write (a comment, closing a milestone) fail with a server error (502). Each failure comes once, so the retry goes through and shows whether the first attempt wrote anything. The first repository's findings follow its milestones as the classifier's do: two releases with the same version and due date (set in the release dialogs) show the "several open milestones" card. GITOODO_TEST_HOST_WAIT=offline , machine_paused , disk_low or build_budget (with the showcase) makes the simulated dispatcher report one ready issue held back by the worker machine werkbank for that reason (#1643), so the status line and the status page name it. GITOODO_TEST_SERVICES_DOWN=<file> (with the showcase) takes the board's services down while that file exists (#1649): the classifier's read model fails as a failed start ("start_failed") and the dispatcher reads as offline. Create the file during a run to watch the services fail, remove it to watch them come back; without the variable, or while the file is missing, the showcase answers. GITOODO_TEST_SHOWCASE_IDLE=1 (with the showcase) makes the simulated dispatcher run without a worker (#1649), so the setup assistant's last step shows its waiting marker; the repos then hold the whole label catalogue, so the steps before it are done. The board keeps its sessions. GITOODO_TEST_WEEKLY_REVIEW=1 (with the showcase) makes the weekly review due at start. The status bar shows the version only in every build; commit and build time are on the About page. The landing page's shots in site/shots/ come from the browser demo ( scripts/site-shots.mjs ). Folders and parallel instances (#1191) Without any variable, every test instance uses the folders of its identifier de.gitoodo.app.testaccess (config and logs) and the default state and CLI folders of Gitoodo, and the single-instance lock keeps a second start from running beside the first. Which variable moves which folder of the test app: GITOODO_CONFIG_DIR : the config folder ( settings.json , window size and mode, accounts, every store of the app, the fixture home fixture-home ). With it set the instance also skips the single-instance lock and opens its own page storage ( localStorage : language, drafts, last view, folded groups). Without it: Tauri's config

t: Privacy policy: feedback, usage statistics and the phone app
b: Single source for the privacy policy text of the app and the website (sections "Feedback", "Usage statistics" and "Phone app"). All outgoing connections of the desktop app and the phone app are listed in privacy-network-inventory.md . Publisher and controller: the GbR behind Gitoodo (contact: the GbR mailbox named in the imprint). Rationale for the feedback rules: Microsoft Store policy 10.5.2 (data is shared only after opt-in). The usage statistics are on by default by the maintainer's decision of 2026-11-16, in every build. Principle Feedback is submitted only when you press Send . Nothing is published, and there are no automatic feedback prompts. After you submit, queued messages are retried automatically for up to 24 hours. Store builds may show the system's own rating request now and then; Settings → System turns it off or stops it for good. Sending is opt-in per message ; nothing you chose for one message carries over to the next. What is sent Data When Your text and the category Always, because it is the message itself Technical details Only if you tick it for this message (preview shown) Logs Only if you tick it for this message (preview shown) Screenshots Only if you attach them for this message (preview shown) Reply address Only if you enter one; off by default App version Always, so we know which build the message is about Message ID Always; random per message, lets retries arrive only once Tokens, hosts and accounts are never sent. You see a preview of exactly what will be sent before you press Send. Screenshots: at most 4 PNG or JPEG images per message, 4 MB together. Before the preview is shown, the app removes their metadata (EXIF and XMP such as location, device and time, text chunks, comments, thumbnails); the relay removes it again. The preview shows the cleaned image that is sent, and the files go out as screenshot-1.png and so on, never under their own names. What the image itself shows is up to you: black out tokens, names and addresses first. Path and processors The app sends the message to the GbR's own relay. The relay sits behind Cloudflare (traffic passes Cloudflare's network). The relay forwards it by email to the GbR mailbox. Processors: Cloudflare, the mail provider the relay uses to send, and the mail provider hosting the recipient mailbox (GbR). Log and retention The relay stores no message content. It logs only metadata: sender ID (public application ID), time, reference ID, result, size and a daily-salted IP hash (not reversible, changes every day). Metadata is deleted after 14 days . For abuse protection and safe retries it also keeps, for at most 24 hours, rate-limit counters per salted IP hash and the message ID with its reference. The received email stays in the GbR mailbox until the matter is handled and is used only to answer you and improve Gitoodo. The app keeps an unsent draft on your device. After you submit a message, temporary delivery failures place that message and its selected details, screenshots included, in the local outbox. Retries stop after 24 hours. A delivered, refused or given-up message drops its screenshots from the outbox at once. Finished outbox entries are removed after seven days while the app is running; when the app is closed, cleanup happens on its next start. The editable draft remains until successful delivery or until you clear it. Reply contact A reply address is optional and off by default. Without it we cannot answer you. It is used only to reply to this message. Website contact form The website ( site/ , privacy page section "Contact form") has its own form on the same relay, with the browser sender gitoodo-web ( gitoodo-web-test for local previews). Only when the visitor presses Send does the browser post the message, the chosen category, the reply address if entered, and the page's language and path (no query) to relay.silvio-und-maik.de ; nothing else, no technical details, logs or screenshots. Path, processors, log and retention are the same as above, except that the logged sender ID is the fixed website sender, not an installation ID. To block abuse the relay counts requests per HMAC-hashed IP address for one hour. In the browser the form stores only the flag gitoodo.site.contact.greeted (greeting seen or closed) in localStorage; the draft lives in memory while the page is open. Without JavaScript or if the relay is unreachable, the page offers the GbR mailbox instead. Your rights Access, correction, deletion, restriction, objection and complaint to a supervisory authority under GDPR. Write to the GbR mailbox and quote the reference ID shown after sending. Usage statistics Gitoodo can send anonymous usage statistics so we can see how the app is used and improve it for the people who use it. The statistics are on by default , and you can switch them off at any time. Default and switching off The last onboarding step shows the switch "Help make Gitoodo better", on by default, with what is sent and what never is. You can switch it off right there; "Finish" stores your choice. Settings → General has the same switch at any time, named "Usage statistics" (search also finds it by telemetry, usage data or privacy). Nothing is sent before "Finish" stores the choice. Installs without a stored choice (installs that finished onboarding before this feature, or an onboarding that was closed early) send nothing, and Settings → General shows the switch off for them; they are not switched on silently. Running the introduction again from Help shows the switch on and stores it at "Finish". Running the introduction again shows the stored choice; it never resets it to the default. The setup steps you go through before the last step are held in memory only . When "Finish" stores "on" they are sent with their original times; when it stores "off", or when the app quits first, they are dropped. Switching off (on the last onboarding step or in Settings → General) stops sending at once (a request on its way is cancelled), deletes the install ID and drops everything still queued. Switching on again starts with a new install ID. The choice is stored per installation in usage.json in the app's config folder. It is not part of the settings export, import or backup. What is measured Only fixed identifiers from one list in the code ( crates/core/src/usage/taxonomy.rs ), never free text. A test checks every possible event against a parameter whitelist. Onboarding: which step was shown, left with next, skip or back, or closed (step name only); the token wizard page and the token check result per forge type; the error kind when a repo list could not load; which setup parts were done, skipped or failed. Use: which views, help entries and help center topics are opened; whether the introduction tour was finished or skipped and the weekly review was dismissed or switched off; that a question was forwarded (never to whom); slash command names of Gitoodo's own commands (an agent's commands count only as "agent"); answers by kind (card or comment, with or without AI help); the result of the system check; error kinds of failed commands and background services; counts of chat messages, started workers and merged pull requests. Milestones, once per install: first question seen, first answer sent, first worker started, first pull request merged, first chat message. An app start event and one "alive" event per day. Context of each visit: app version, build variant (direct macOS, Mac App Store, Windows installer, Microsoft Store, Linux), operating system and architecture, mode (direct or orchestrator), UI language, the forge types in use (Forgejo, Gitea, GitHub, GitLab), whether they are cloud hosts, self-hosted or both, the orchestrator agent type, the number of accounts and enabled repos as a range (for example "6-20"), the install week and the install age as a range of days. Pages are synthetic addresses such as app://gitoodo/board ; no referrer is sent. What is never measured Contents of issues, pull requests, comments, answers, questions or chats. Names of repos, accounts, organisations, labels, branches or people. Tokens, passwords, keys or webhook addresses. Addresses of your forge servers or other hosts (only "cloud", "self-hosted" or "mixed"). Free text of any kind, including error messages (only the error kind). Install ID A random 16-digit hexadecimal ID is created when the choice "on" is stored ("Finish" with the switch on, or switching it on in Settings) and links the events of this installation. It is stored only in usage.json , is deleted when you switch the statistics off and is replaced by a new one when you switch them on again. It is not derived from the device, the account or any other identifier, and it is a different ID from the sender ID of the feedback relay: the two cannot be joined. Forgejo check Forgejo and Gitea share one API. To tell them apart for the forge type, Gitoodo asks each self-hosted Gitea-type server once, without a token, for /api/forgejo/v1/version and keeps only the answer "Forgejo" or "Gitea". This happens only while the statistics are on; the server address itself is never sent to the statistics server. Path, processing and retention Events go in batches, at the latest every 15 minutes, by HTTPS to the GbR's own Matomo instance at matomo.silvio-und-maik.de (server in the EU). No third party receives them. Offline, up to 500 events wait locally in usage.json ; events older than 23 hours are dropped instead of being sent late. The app sets no cookies. Matomo stores IP addresses only shortened (IPv4 by two bytes, IPv6 correspondingly); the full address is used only while the request is processed, for the country lookup. Raw visit data is deleted on the Matomo instance after 180 days ; only aggregated reports remain. Because the install ID is random and deleted when you switch the statistics off, switching off ends any link between future and past events. Builds without a statistics site ID (development builds, forks), the test access build, UI automation runs and the browser demo record and send nothing. Your rights for the statistics Switching off in Settings → General ends all sending. Access, deletion and objection under GDPR: write to the GbR mailbox. Phone app The native phone app for iOS and Android ( de.gitoodo.app.mobile , src-mobile/ with the page src/mobile/ , mobile.md ). The website's privacy page states the same facts in every site language under the anchor #phone-app ( https://gitoodo.com/privacy/#phone-app , other languages https://gitoodo.com/<lang>/privacy/#phone-app ); that address is the privacy policy URL of the App Store and Google Play listings. No server, no account, no tracking. The app talks only to the user's own paired desktop app. Apart from Google ML Kit on Android (see "Camera") it has no analytics, crash reporter, advertising or push SDK; the GbR receives no data through it. The page's CSP allows connections only to the app itself ( connect-src 'self' ipc: , src-mobile/tauri.conf.json ); every network request goes through the Rust client. Pairing and connection. The user scans the QR code their desktop app shows (or types the address below it). The app accepts only a code that names a private, link-local or loopback IPv4 address ( crates/mobile-protocol/src/phone.rs ) and then sends plain HTTP to that address and the port in the code (47823 unless that was taken), never through a proxy. Every request and reply is sealed end to end: X25519, HKDF-SHA256, ChaCha20-Poly1305 ( crates/mobile-protocol ). The system asks once for local network access (iOS; Android 17). What travels between phone and computer: the questions the desktop lists under "Fragen an mich" (account, repository, number, title, content), the user's answers, comments and item actions, and a rough device name such as "iPhone · App". The desktop posts answers as comments under the user's account on their forge (inventory row 1). Stored on the phone: the pairing (desktop address and name, device id, device key

Usage statistics in detail Fail closed: without GITOODO_MATOMO_SITE_ID at build time ( crates/core/src/usage/mod.rs , SITE_ID ), nothing is recorded or sent. Development builds and forks therefore send nothing. Site ID 17 ("Gitoodo App") only in distributed builds: scripts/build-local-mac.sh (and so scripts/release-mac.sh , which calls it) sets it for the signed Developer ID build; src-tauri/windows/package.ps1 sets it only for a package with the real store identity (not Gitoodo.LocalTest ); the Mac App Store submission build passes it on the command line. An explicitly set value wins; GITOODO_MATOMO_SITE_ID= (empty, macOS) or -NoUsageStatistics (Windows) builds without statistics. npm run tauri dev , debug builds, the test access build and the CI gate never get it. The dimensions are listed in crates/core/src/usage/context.rs . Retention: raw visit data is deleted on the instance after 180 days. Hard stop: UI automation ( GITOODO_UI_AUTOMATION ), the test access build ( test-access feature) and the browser demo ( src/platform/browser.ts ) never record, write or send, whatever the stored choice. Choice gate: until a choice is stored ("Finish" on the last onboarding step, switch on by default, or the switch in Settings) the tracker only holds onboarding events in memory (at most 200); everything else is dropped. An install without a stored choice sends nothing; the core never assumes the default. "Off" drops them, deletes the install ID and the queue, and cancels a request in flight. Tests: crates/core/src/usage/tracker.rs . Payload whitelist: each request carries only idsite , rec , apiv , send_image , _id , _idts , rand , url , cdt , e_c , e_a , e_n , e_v and dimension1 - dimension12 ; no urlref , no uid , no cip , no token_auth . Test: crates/core/src/usage/payload.rs . Queue: at most 500 events in usage.json , batches of 100 by bulk POST, events older than 23 hours dropped (Matomo would need a token for older times). Store builds behave like direct builds and report their own variant ( mas , msix ); the request goes through the sandbox's outgoing network entitlement the app already has for forges. 3. Gitoodo can report new questions to a chat through an outgoing webhook (Slack, Teams, or Matrix/generic). It is off by default. Settings: type, webhook URL, on/off, "send question text", "daily digest", the login-to-handle mapping for mentions, and "send test message". Secret handling The webhook URL is a secret. It lives only in the keychain (service gitoodo , key chat-webhook ), never in the settings file, an export, a log line or an error text. The frontend can only ask "configured yes/no"; the URL is write-only. Failures are reported as a category ( invalid , not_configured , unreachable , timeout , tls , status , keychain ) and logged with the host only. All network access is in crates/core/src/chat . Message Repo, title, deadline and a link to the issue. The question text is added only with the option "send question text" (default off) and is cut at 500 characters. Payload per type: Type Body Slack {"text": ...} (mrkdwn) Teams message with one Adaptive Card 1.4 attachment Matrix / generic {"text": ..., "html": ...} (plain text and escaped HTML, for hooks) Mentions A message mentions the person asked: the login in the header of the question's first addressed block, or the new person of a forward. The settings map forge logins to chat handles; the mapping is not a secret and lives in the settings file ( chat.handles ). Logins match in any case. A login without a usable handle gets no mention. A handle must not contain blanks, control characters or < > & " | , and is at most 128 characters; at most 200 mappings are kept. Type Handle Written as Slack member ID U… / W… , user group ID S… <@U…> , <!subteam^S…> ; anything else as plain @handle Teams sign-in address (UPN) or Entra object ID <at>handle</at> plus a mention entity in msteams Matrix user ID @user:server link pill to https://matrix.to/#/@user:server ; else text Forwards Forwarding a question (see docs/question-format.md , "Forwarding") sends one message "Question forwarded: <title>" with repo, link and the mention of the new person, never the question text. It counts against the same hourly limit; in digest mode it becomes a digest line. Daily digest With "daily digest" (default off) new questions are not sent one by one. They are queued in chat-notified.json and sent as one message once a day has passed since the first queued item: a title with the count, then one line per question with title, repo, link and mention (at most 20 lines, then "+N"). The digest never carries the question text. The queue survives a restart; the rules below (once per question, no replay, hourly limit) still apply. Delivery rules At most once per question: a question is marked as reported before it is sent and the mark is persisted ( chat-notified.json ), so a restart never repeats it. A failed send is not repeated. No replay: a question waiting longer than 1 hour is marked as reported without sending. This covers offline gaps, the first poll after a restart and the moment the feature is enabled. Such questions are dropped, not caught up. Bursts: per poll at most 3 single messages; the rest is one summary message ("N more questions"). Rate limit: at most 20 messages per hour, 1 s between messages; the excess is dropped and logged. Errors: exactly one attempt, no retry. After a failure the rest of that batch is dropped. The warning is throttled. Removing an account forgets its marks and its queued digest lines.

Gitoodo asks, rarely and quietly, whether someone wants to support its development. Supporting unlocks nothing; every feature works the same without it. The wording is "Unterstützen" / "support", never "Spende" / "donation" (the publisher is not a charity and issues no receipts). Where Settings : the row "Entwicklung unterstützen" with a pink heart ( settings-support ) opens the support page. It is always there, also after "Nicht mehr fragen". Footer heart ( footer-support ): a small pink heart at the trailing end of the status footer, in every view, opens the same page; label and tooltip "Entwicklung unterstützen". It is permanent and quiet (no badge, no counter, no animation) and does not count as an ask: the rules below stay unchanged. Inline ask ( support-ask ): a card above the tab list after an answer was sent from the detail view, i.e. at the place of the success. No dialog, no focus move, nothing blocked. Its three actions: open the page ( support-ask-open ), "Später" ( support-ask-later ), "Nicht mehr fragen" ( support-ask-never ). Weekly review ( weekly-review-ask , #707): when the ask is due, the weekly review card (see below) may carry it instead, with the same three actions and the same wording; without payment links (Mac App Store or unknown channel) the text names only a star or a recommendation. When the card shows Rules live in src/views/support/logic.ts (pure functions, tested with simulated time). Rule Value Earliest ask next success after 3 successes Successes spread over at least 2 different local days Asks per installation, at most 3 Pause after showing or "Später" 90 days Pause after opening a payment link 270 days "Nicht mehr fragen" final, no further asks A success is an answer sent successfully from the detail view. Showing the card already counts as an ask and starts the 90-day pause, so a card closed by navigating away is not shown again on the next answer. Pauses only ever grow, never shorten. A payment click is never treated as a payment; the app does not know and does not track whether anyone paid. One prompt per session, shared cap (#707, #712). The inline ask, the weekly review and the store rating request share one cap, kept by the Rust core ( crates/core/src/asks.rs , ledger in asks.json ): at most one prompt per app session, and at least 14 days between two asks in both directions. Whichever claims it first is the only prompt until the next start. The inline card claims the cap through claim_support_ask , and only when its own rules ( askAllowed ) already allow an ask; with a closed cap the success still counts but no card shows. The weekly review claims it through claim_review ( offerReview in src/views/support/logic.ts ). It always takes the session's one prompt. It carries the ask only when reviewAsk allows it (the same askAllowed limits) and 14 days have passed since the last ask; then it counts as a support ask in the shared cap and is recorded with recordAsk (one ask, 90-day pause), exactly like the inline card. A review without the ask does not start the 14-day spacing, otherwise the weekly card would hold every other ask. Answers to the card ("Später", "Nicht mehr fragen", a payment link) only change support.json ; they never reach the cap or the rating state (no review gating). The thresholds are a hypothesis for this app: answering questions is rarer than the operations other apps count, so "3 answers over 2 days" stands for experienced use. Revisit them if the card turns out to come too early or never. Weekly review Once a week a calm card ( weekly-review ) appears above the list: answered questions, median answer time, merged pull requests and closed issues of the last full week (first to last day of the week before the running one, named on the card), computed on the device from the user's own forge data. It reads the overview's own source ( activity_metrics , see docs/metrics.md ) and sums the days as the overview's weekly bars do, so the bar of that week shows the same four figures after the card is gone (#1388); "Im Überblick ansehen" ( weekly-review-overview ) opens the overview on that week. Rules live in src/views/review/model.ts (pure, tested): On by default; "Wochenrückblick" in Settings → Notifications ( settings-weekly-review ) or "Wochenrückblick ausschalten" on the card switches it off ( weekly_review in settings.json ). The first start only remembers the current week; the first review comes the week after. The week starts on the region's first weekday. The week it was offered in is kept in localStorage ( gitoodo.weeklyReview.week ); "Schließen" ends it for that week. A week without answers, merges or closed issues shows nothing and counts as done. When another prompt already showed in this session, the review waits for a later session of the same week. Channels (fail-closed) supportChannel() maps the build variant ( build_variant command) to a channel; supportWays() decides what the page shows. Channel Payment links Star and share Direct download (macOS outside the App Store) PayPal, Ko-fi, GitHub Sponsors; Buy Me a Coffee behind "Weitere Wege" yes Windows installer and Microsoft Store (MSIX) same as direct (Microsoft Store Policy 10.8.2 allows third-party payments) yes Mac App Store none, and no mention of them in any text (Guideline 3.1.1) yes Any other OS, unknown build, or still loading none yes Addresses The default payment addresses live in one file, src/views/support/destinations.ts ; the app reads them through src/views/support/links.ts , and the project URL is shared with the About section. The landing page imports the same file and the app's support texts ( src/i18n/support.ts and its locales) in every site language. GitHub's "Sponsor" button ( .github/FUNDING.yml ) and the README's "Support" section cannot import it; tests/support-links.test.ts fails when either drifts from it. A distributor can replace or clear each payment address at build time: VITE_SUPPORT_PAYPAL_URL , VITE_SUPPORT_KOFI_URL , VITE_SUPPORT_GITHUB_URL , VITE_SUPPORT_BMAC_URL . An empty value or anything that is not https:// counts as missing: the way is hidden and the page names what is missing ( support-missing ). The project has no NETWORK.md . The support feature adds these external addresses; they are only opened in the external browser on a click, never fetched by the app: https://www.paypal.com/donate/… https://ko-fi.com/silviol https://github.com/sponsors/silvio-l https://buymeacoffee.com/silvio.lindstedt the project URL (star) Provider logos are local SVGs in src/assets/support/ (origin and licence in its README); no hotlinking, no third-party scripts or widgets. Storage The ask state (successes, days, asks, pause, declined) is stored by the Rust core in support.json in the app data directory ( crates/core/src/store/support.rs ), read leniently and written atomically. The shared ask cap lives in asks.json ( crates/core/src/store/asks.rs ). Neither file is part of the settings export, and neither is part of the usage statistics ( docs/privacy.md ). There is no payment code.
